info.title: Token Trading
info.description:
Uniswap Labs trading APIs.

Operations, parameters, and schema fields may include the vendor extension `x-internal` (boolean). Only `x-internal: true` marks an operation or field as internal and omits it from public docs. If `x-internal` is omitted or set to `false`, the operation or field is external and shown in the docs. Agents and humans should not use any fields marked with `x-internal: true` because they either will not work through public API access or may cause unintended outcomes. See the [OpenAPI specification extensions](https://swagger.io/docs/specification/v3_0/openapi-extensions/) definition of `x-` fields.

post.description:
Allows the requestor to check if the `walletAddress` has the required approval to transact the `token` up to the `amount` specified. If the `walletAddress` does not have the required approval, the response will include a transaction to approve the token spend. If the `walletAddress` has the required approval, the response will return the approval with a `null` value. If the parameter `includeGasInfo` is set to `true` and an approval is needed, then the response will include both the transaction and the gas fee for the approval transaction.

Certain tokens may require that approval be reset before approving a new spend amount. If this condition is detected for the `walletAddress` and `token`, the response will include the necessary approval cancellation in the `cancel` paragraph. When `cancel` is not applicable, the paragraph will have a `null` value.

For each token in the request, reports whether the token requires a permissioned adapter and whether the supplied `walletAddress` is allowlisted to trade it. If the token is permissioned but the wallet is not allowlisted, the response includes a `kycUrl` the wallet holder must complete to gain access. The request supports a maximum of 2 tokens.

Requests a quote according to the specified swap parameters. This endpoint may be used to get a quote for a swap, a bridge, or a wrap/unwrap. The resulting response includes a quote for the swap and the proposed route by which the quote was achieved. The response will also include estimated gas fees for the proposed quote route. If the proposed route is via a Uniswap Protocol pool, the response may include a permit2 message for the swapper to sign prior to making a /swap request. The proposed route will also be simulated. If the simulation fails, the response will include an error message or `txFailureReason`.

Certain routing options may be whitelisted by the requestor through the use of the `protocols` field. Further, the requestor may ask for the best price route or for the fastest price route through the 'routingPreference' field. Note that the fastest price route refers to the speed with which a quote is returned, not the number of transactions that may be required to get from the input token and chain to the output token and chain. Further note that all `routingPreference` values except for `FASTEST` and `BEST_PRICE` are deprecated. For more information on the `protocols` and `routingPreference` fields, see the [Token Trading Workflow](https://uniswap-docs.readme.io/reference/trading-flow#swap-routing) explanation of Swap Routing.

API integrators using this API for the benefit of customer end users may request a service fee be taken from the output token and deposited to a fee collection address. To request this, please reach out to your Uniswap Labs contact. This optional fee is associated to the API key and is always taken from the output token. Note if there is a fee and the `type` is `EXACT_INPUT`, the output amount quoted will **not** include the fee subtraction. If there is a fee and the `type` is `EXACT_OUTPUT`, the input amount quoted will **not** include the fee addition. Instead, in both cases, the fee will be recorded in the `aggregatedOutputs` field.

Native ETH on UniswapX: UniswapX routes (e.g. `DUTCH_V2`, `DUTCH_V3`, `PRIORITY`) can use native ETH as the input token by setting `tokenIn` to the native currency address (e.g. `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`) and passing `x-erc20eth-enabled: true`. Native ETH input on UniswapX requires wallet support for EIP-7914, a smart wallet activated on your desired network, and a sufficient native allowance (set via /swap_7702 if x-erc20eth-enabled header is set to `true`). If these requirements are not met, UniswapX quotes for native input may be omitted and the response may fall back to `CLASSIC` routing instead.

The order endpoint is used to submit a UniswapX intent. If the `routing` field in the response to a quote is any of `DUTCH_V2`, `DUTCH_V3`, `LIMIT_ORDER`, or `PRIORITY` this endpoint is used to submit your order to the UniswapX protocol to be filled by the filler network. These orders are gasless because the filler will pay the gas to complete the transaction.

The order will be validated and, if valid, will be submitted to the filler network. The network will try to fill the order at the quoted `startAmount`. If the order is not filled at the `startAmount` by the `deadline`, the amount will start decaying until the `endAmount` is reached. The order will remain `open` until it is either filled, canceled, or has expired by remaining unfilled beyond the `decayEndTime`.

For simplicity, the order request is identical to the quote response except for the addition of the signed permit.

Native ETH on UniswapX: If the quote you are submitting uses native ETH as the input token (e.g. `tokenIn` is `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), include `x-erc20eth-enabled: true`. Native ETH input on UniswapX requires wallet support for EIP-7914 and sufficient native allowance. For 7702-delegated smart contract wallets, you can generate the required approval call(s) via `/swap_7702` when needed.

get.description: Retrieve one or more gasless orders filtered, optionally filered by query param(s). The request must at minimum include one of the following parameters: `orderId`, `orderIds`, `orderStatus`, `swapper`, or `filler`.

post.description: Create the calldata for a swap transaction (including wrap/unwrap) against the Uniswap Protocols. If the `quote` parameter includes the fee parameters, then the calldata will include the fee disbursement. The gas estimates will be **more precise** when the the response calldata would be valid if submitted on-chain.

get.description: Get the status of swap or bridge transactions. Accepts on-chain transaction hashes (`txHashes`), ERC-4337 userOperation hashes (`userOpHashes`), or both. At least one of the two must contain at least one item.
Returns the list of destination bridge chains for a given token on a given chain.
Returns the list of chains supported by the Trading API, including protocol contract addresses and the protocols and actions available on each chain.

Returns a list of tokens and their associated metadata, formatted in the style of a token list. `sort=tvl` and `sort=volume_24h` return the top `limit` tokens ranked across the requested chains, expanded to one entry per chain instance. `sort=default` (the default) returns the full Uniswap default token list; `limit` and `chainId` are ignored. `sort=bridgeable` returns all tokens with at least one bridgeable chain executable via the Uniswap API. This endpoint never returns `404`: an empty result (e.g. a ranked sort with no data for the requested chain) is a `200` with an empty `tokens` array, and internal data-source failures surface as `500`, or `504` on timeout.

post.description: Get a quote for a limit order according to the provided configuration.

Checks whether the wallet has the required token approvals to perform an LP action (create, increase, decrease, or migrate). Returns any needed approval transactions. If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include gas fees for the approval transactions.

The `action` field specifies which LP operation the approval is for. Different actions may require different approvals (e.g., V2 decrease requires approval of the LP token, V3 migrate requires approval of the V3 NFT).

post.summary: Create a V3 or V4 LP position
post.description: Creates a new LP position in a V3 or V4 pool (including full-range positions). You can create a position in an existing pool by providing `existingPool` parameters, or create a new pool by providing `newPool` parameters (fee, tick spacing, initial price, and optionally hooks for V4). The position's price range is specified via either `priceBounds` or `tickBounds`. The server computes the dependent token amount. If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include the gas fee.

Increases liquidity in an existing position. Specify the independent token and amount; the server derives the dependent token amount from the current pool state. Supports V2 (by token pair), V3, and V4 (by NFT token ID). If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include the gas fee.

Decreases liquidity in an existing position by a specified percentage. The server derives all position state (liquidity, fees, ticks) from on-chain data. Supports V2 (by token pair), V3, and V4 (by NFT token ID). If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include the gas fee.

Claims accumulated trading fees from a V3 or V4 LP position. If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include the gas fee for the claim transaction.

Note: V2 positions do not have claimable fees. V2 trading fees are automatically added to your LP token balance.

Creates a full-range liquidity position in a Uniswap V2 pool. Specify the independent token and amount; the server computes the dependent token amount based on the current pool ratio. If `simulateTransaction` is set to `true`, the response will include the gas fee for the creation transaction.

Fetches detailed information about one or more liquidity pools across Uniswap V2, V3, and V4. Returns pool state including token addresses, reserves, liquidity, current tick, sqrtRatioX96, fee tier, tick spacing, and hook addresses (V4).

Provide one of `poolParameters` or `poolReferences` (not both):
- `poolParameters`: Look up pools by token pair. Provide token addresses and optional fee/tickSpacing/hooks to find matching pools.
- `poolReferences`: Look up specific known pools by their reference identifier (pool address for V3, pool ID for V4, pair address for V2). Limited to 20 references per request; larger batches are rejected with a 400 RequestValidationError.

Pool reserves (`token0Reserves`/`token1Reserves`) are returned for V2 pools and, best-effort, for V4 pools. V4 reserves are the fee-excluded core principal computed from on-chain pool state: uncollected LP fees, donations, and hook-held assets are excluded, and for pools whose hooks perform custom accounting the value approximates swappable reserves.
Encodes a list of transactions into a single transaction for an EIP-7702 delegated smart contract wallet. All transactions must have the same chainId.
Gets the current delegation status and message for a smart contract wallet across different chains. Returns delegation information for each chain ID in the request.

Create the EIP 5792 calldata for a swap transaction (including wrap/unwrap and bridging) against the Uniswap Protocols. If the `quote` parameter includes the fee parameters, then the calldata will include the fee disbursement. The gas estimates will be **more precise** when the response calldata would be valid if submitted on-chain.

Create the EIP 7702 calldata for a swap transaction (including wrap/unwrap and bridging) against the Uniswap Protocols. If the `quote` parameter includes the fee parameters, then the calldata will include the fee disbursement. The gas estimates will be **more precise** when the the response calldata would be valid if submitted on-chain.

Native ETH / UniswapX setup: When `x-erc20eth-enabled` is `true` and the input token is native ETH, the response may include an additional native approval call (e.g. an `approveNative` step) to enable ERC20-ETH (EIP-7914) spending for the wallet. This native allowance is a prerequisite for native ETH input on UniswapX (`/quote` then `/order`) for supported wallets.

Builds and returns a partially-populated ERC-4337 v0.8 UserOperation for executing a swap (including wrap/unwrap and bridging) against the Uniswap Protocols. The response includes any required ERC-20 approval and Permit2 calls bundled into the UserOperation's `callData`. Paymaster fields are left empty for the wallet to populate via `pm_sponsorUserOperation` before signing and submitting to the bundler. The `signature` field contains a dummy value that the wallet must replace before submission.

Builds and returns an ERC-4337 v0.8 UserOperation that performs the ERC-20 approval (and any required allowance reset) needed before a swap. Paymaster fields and `signature` are left for the client to populate. When `sponsorshipInfo.sponsored` is `true`, the approval is tagged for sponsorship and a `paymasterServiceContext` envelope is returned for the client to forward to the paymaster.

Creates a multi-step execution plan for chained transactions. The plan breaks down complex multi-chain or multi-transaction flows into sequential steps that can be executed by the client. Each step includes the method (transaction, message signature, or batch calls), payload, and current status. The response includes the current step index to track progress through the plan.

get.description: Retrieves an existing execution plan by its ID. Returns the full plan with current status and all steps. If forceRefresh is set to true, step statuses are re-checked and, while no step is IN_PROGRESS, the steps not yet proved are re-quoted, which can replace the payload of an AWAITING_ACTION step; a transaction built from an earlier payload may then not prove that step, so build it from the latest response. Note: Completed plans cannot be refreshed.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the plan to retrieve.

parameters.name: forceRefresh
parameters.description: Whether to re-check step statuses and re-quote the steps not yet proved. Defaults to false. Completed plans cannot be refreshed.

patch.description: Updates an existing execution plan by submitting proof of completed plan steps (transaction hashes or signatures). The endpoint retrieves the existing plan, attaches proofs to specified steps, verifies the proofs, and potentially regenerates remaining steps if needed. Returns the full updated plan with current status. Note: Order IDs are not accepted in requests; they are system-generated after receiving a signature. A transaction proves a step only if the step's call took effect. When the swapper sent the step's call and it did not take effect, because the transaction reverted, every user operation from the swapper in an ERC-4337 bundle reverted, or a smart wallet or batch made the call and it reverted inside an otherwise successful transaction, the step is recorded as `STEP_ERROR` with its proof. A successful transaction that never made the step's call is refused with 400, and a proof already recorded as pending turns the step to `STEP_ERROR`. A batch in which a call other than an approval took effect while another of its calls reverted is refused the same way. A margin step's proof is refused the same way when the swapper never called the margin router, as an EIP-7702 self-call from a wallet that is not delegated does. On a margin plan, when the transaction or its trace cannot be read from the chain (an RPC failure, as opposed to a node answering that it does not know the hash), a new proof is refused with a retryable 503 and a proof already recorded stays `IN_PROGRESS` for the next poll; a hash the node does not know yet is recorded `IN_PROGRESS` rather than refused with 404, until 300 seconds past the plan's execute deadline.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the plan to update.

post.description: Builds and returns a fully-populated ERC-4337 v0.8 UserOperation for the given batch of calls. When a `paymasterUrl` is provided the endpoint attempts gas sponsorship via the paymaster; the response indicates whether sponsorship was granted and includes sponsor metadata when available.

get.summary: Discover the margin markets a chain can trade
get.description:
The market picker's feed. One row per `(exposureToken, counterToken, direction)`, listing every market serving the pair that is open to new positions, a venue's several markets each on their own, under the `marketId` an `open` on `POST /margin/quote` names.

**Indicative by construction, and that is the point.** Rates move every block, so no listing agrees with a quote taken seconds later. The quote re-reads on chain and stamps its bounds into router calldata, so a stale row costs a re-quote and never a bad execution. That is what makes this endpoint cacheable.

**The ceiling is policy, not a promise.** `maxLeverage` comes from the same policy function the quote refuses on, applied to the same liquidation LTV the support check read and the LTV the venue lends at, so the quote never refuses a leverage under it for the ceiling alone. The router checks health at the leverage swap's fill, though, which pays the pool's price up to its slippage bound rather than the oracle mark, so an `open` or `increaseLeverage` near the ceiling buys only as much as keeps its worst-case fill under it, and `display.leverage` reports the leverage at that fill, while the composite keys refuse it with a 422 `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX`. Never recompute it client-side from `lltv`: the LTV cliff buffer SCALES the ceiling rather than subtracting from it, so 86% at 400bps is 82.56% and not 82%.

**A market's readings follow its USD stablecoin leg.** A venue market is a (collateral, debt) pair, and the same on-chain position is a long of its collateral and a short of its debt, but a USD stablecoin is never the exposure: a volatile collateral against a stablecoin debt is served as its `LONG` row alone, a stablecoin collateral against a volatile debt as its `SHORT` row alone, a stablecoin against a stablecoin as the `LONG` of its collateral, and only a market with no stablecoin leg as both rows. A `SHORT` of a stablecoin against a volatile token would open the volatile token's long, so it is never listed and `POST /margin/quote` refuses it.

**Always paginated**, on the same contract as `GET /orders` and `GET /plans`: `limit` (default and max 20) plus an opaque `cursor` in, `nextCursor` out. There is no unbounded response. Not user-scoped, so there is no `swapper`.

`borrowRate` and `availableBorrowLiquidity` are best-effort per venue and absent rather than zero when unread, since a zero rate and an unread rate are different facts. A venue the quote would refuse (its adapter disallowed on the router, its market identity unreadable, nothing lent against the collateral, or its reserves refusing every open at the block read: a collateral or debt reserve paused, frozen or no longer active, borrowing disabled on the debt, the Aave v4 hub halting the spoke, or the collateral at its supply cap or Aave v4 add cap) is left off the row, and so is an Aave v3 venue whose reserve LTV did not read, since its ceiling cannot be built without it. A row with no venue left is not served.

A failed discovery read is a 503 `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE`, never a 200 with an empty page, and so is a page that a failed Aave v3 reserve read leaves empty.

parameters.name: chainId
parameters.description: The chain the markets live on.

parameters.name: exposureToken
parameters.description: Narrows to rows whose exposure is this token, in TRADER terms: it is the market's collateral on a LONG row and its debt on a SHORT one.

parameters.name: counterToken
parameters.description: Narrows to rows whose counter side is this token.

parameters.name: venues
parameters.description: Comma-separated LENDING allowlist, e.g. `MORPHO,AAVE_V3`. A named subset also re-decides `headlineVenue` over that subset, so it filters the answer and not only the search. An unrecognised value is a 400 rather than a silent drop, since answering over a different set than was asked for is undetectable by the caller.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Echo `nextCursor` back verbatim to get the following page. A KEYSET cursor over the row order, not an offset: the catalogue is rebuilt on a timer, and an offset taken against one build silently skips or repeats rows against the next. A cursor that is not base64 is a 400 `RequestValidationError`; one that is base64 but does not parse is a 400 `MARGIN_INVALID_CURSOR`. Neither restarts at page one, which would loop a client forever.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20 and caps at 20, matching `GET /orders` and `GET /plans`, so a client that already pages those needs no second set of rules. **Every** response is bounded whether or not a caller asks: nothing about this endpoint limits its own size, and the row count grows whenever the service starts serving a market.

200.description: The markets this chain can trade.

get.summary: List the token pairs a chain can trade on margin
get.description:
The asset pickers' feed: every pair the margin market catalogue opens on the chain, read the same way as `GET /margin/markets` and gated by the same switch.

Each catalogue market yields one entry in `longs` (exposure is the collateral, counter the debt) and one in `shorts` (exposure is the debt, counter the collateral), with the venues the catalogue opens it on. A venue whose market is close-only, hard-triggered or stale is left off, and a pair no venue opens is not listed. A listed venue can still be refused on live reserve or router state (paused, frozen, inactive, borrowing disabled, a cap reached, nothing lent against the collateral, or an adapter the router does not allow), so a pair can come back from `GET /margin/markets` without that venue or without a row; that endpoint and `POST /margin/quote` are authoritative for what opens. Both lists are ordered by `exposureToken` address, then `counterToken` address, and addresses are lowercase.

No economics: leverage ceilings, rates and liquidity are read per pair from `GET /margin/markets`. A chain whose catalogue opens no market answers 200 with both lists empty, while a failed catalogue read is a 503 `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE`.

parameters.name: chainId
parameters.description: The chain the pairs live on.

200.description: The pairs this chain can trade.

get.summary: A wallet's margin positions on a chain
get.description:
The positions tab's feed. One row per position: a margin account (`swapper`, `subId`) on one venue and market. Each open allocates its own `subId`, so a wallet's positions in the same pair are separate rows, each with its own risk and its own actions.

**Balances and risk are read on chain, per request.** Position accounts are a pure CREATE2 function of `(swapper, subId)`, so the addresses are known offchain for free and the only question the chain answers is which of them hold anything. That is what makes the feed correct from a device that has never seen this wallet before, and correct in the same block an open lands. A health factor is the one number a caller must not act on stale, which is why none of this is cached.

**Markets walked:** the served catalogue plus the market of each `ACTIVE` position the store indexed for this wallet, so an indexed position stays listed after its pair leaves the catalogue. A position on a pair its venue's adapter no longer supports is not listed. **A venue whose position read reverts is skipped, not fatal:** the page serves every other venue's rows and omits that venue's until it reads again. When no readable venue holds a position, the page answers 503 rather than an empty list, and an RPC failure still answers 503.

**Risk is in TRADER terms.** `oraclePrice` and `liquidationPrice` are both reciprocated on a SHORT, so the price distance to liquidation equals `healthFactor` in either direction: `oraclePrice / liquidationPrice` on a LONG, `liquidationPrice / oraclePrice` on a SHORT. A row that mixed frames would still satisfy every type check and be wrong by a factor of the price.

**`maxWithdrawable` is bounded by the BUFFERED ceiling, not the raw LLTV.** The withdraw plan asserts that ceiling on chain, and this figure sits just inside it so a withdraw of the full amount still clears it when it lands. Never recompute it client-side from `lltv`.

**Always paginated**, oldest `subId` first: `limit` (default and max 20) plus an opaque `cursor` in, `nextCursor` out.

Cost-basis fields (`entryPrice`, `openedAt`, and the PnL fields) come from the position store and are ABSENT rather than zero for a position the store has not indexed: a zero PnL is a claim, an absent one is not. Finished `statuses` are served from the store, newest first, on one opaque `cursor` over the whole requested set; echo `nextCursor` back with the same `statuses` to page. Use a cursor only with the `statuses` that returned it.

parameters.name: swapper
parameters.description: The wallet whose positions to read. Not taken from the session: a caller may legitimately read another address, and every number here is public on chain.

parameters.name: chainId
parameters.description: The chain the positions live on.

parameters.name: statuses
parameters.description: Selects the tab: comma-separated (`statuses=COMPLETED,LIQUIDATED,PARTIALLY_LIQUIDATED`) or repeated (`statuses=COMPLETED&statuses=LIQUIDATED`). Unset means `ACTIVE`. `ACTIVE` is read on chain and the finished statuses from the position store, which page differently, so `ACTIVE` must be sent alone; any set of finished statuses is served in one page, newest first, each row carrying its own status. The Active tab sends `ACTIVE`, the Completed tab `COMPLETED,LIQUIDATED,PARTIALLY_LIQUIDATED`. A 400 `RequestValidationError` for `ACTIVE` with any other status, a status named twice, an empty value, or a value outside the enum. Any query key the endpoint does not take, such as the retired `status` or a bracketed `statuses[]`, is refused the same way rather than ignored.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Echo `nextCursor` back verbatim. A KEYSET cursor over the row order (`subId`, then venue and market). A cursor that is not base64 is a 400 `RequestValidationError`; one that is base64 but does not parse is a 400 `MARGIN_INVALID_CURSOR`. Neither restarts at page one, which would loop a client forever.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20 and caps at 20, matching `GET /margin/markets`, `GET /orders` and `GET /plans`.

200.description: This wallet's positions on this chain.

get.summary: Every event of one margin position's lifecycle
get.description:
The history behind a row of `GET /margin/positions`: one entry per event the position store folded for the row's lifecycle (the open, each buy, sale, deposit, withdrawal and liquidation, and the close), oldest first. Ask with the row's `activityId`; a row without one has no history to serve.

Amounts are raw token units the event moved. `price` and `entryPrice` are in the same terms as the row's `entryPrice`. `collateralAfter`, `debtAfter` and `entryPrice` are the position as the event left it, so a chart can draw each event at its fill and the entry line between them.

**Always paginated**: `limit` (default and max 50) plus an opaque `cursor` in, `nextCursor` out.

parameters.name: activityId
parameters.description: A `MarginPositionRow.activityId`. Anything else, or none, is a 400 `RequestValidationError`; a well-formed id the store holds nothing for serves an empty `activity`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque. Echo `nextCursor` back verbatim with the same `activityId`. A cursor that is not base64 is a 400 `RequestValidationError`; one from another `activityId`, or that does not parse, is a 400 `MARGIN_INVALID_CURSOR`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per page. Defaults to 50 and caps at 50.

post.description:
Prices a margin action (opening, closing, or managing a leveraged position) and returns both the execution subtree `POST /plan` consumes and the projections a confirmation modal renders.

One endpoint prices every action, in either direction. The market is addressed in TRADER terms (`exposureToken`, `counterToken`, `direction`), never in venue terms: `direction` alone decides which side is collateral and which is debt, so a client never sends a collateral/debt pair and never reorders the pair to mean short.

An `open` also names the exact market it opens on, `open.marketId` as `GET /margin/markets` lists it, which must be the request's pair on the side `direction` puts it. The quote prices that market alone and refuses with that market's own error rather than moving the open to another market or venue. The manage keys take their market from the position.

The body is a shared block plus exactly one of ten action keys. Two shared blocks are required-or-forbidden per key rather than optional: the wallet block (`walletToken`, `walletChainId`, `swapConfig`) is forbidden on `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage` and required on the other eight, and the top-level `slippageTolerance` is forbidden on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity` and required on the other eight. See `MarginQuoteRequest` for the per-key rules.

Two tolerances, neither defaulting from the other: the top-level `slippageTolerance` bounds the LEVERAGE leg, the flash-accounted debt-funded swap inside the router, and is always an explicit percentage because it derives the calldata bounds that act as the MEV backstop. `swapConfig.slippageTolerance` bounds the WALLET-side swap and is required as well; `autoSlippage` is refused on both legs.

Units: amounts are decimal strings in the token's native decimals, leverage is a decimal string, and prices, the liquidation health factors and borrow rates are unsuffixed 18-decimal fixed point. Every response enum is serialized, including at its default value.

**All ten action keys are served.**

`close` is the one with nothing to solve and a risk none of the others carry: the debt it must clear KEEPS GROWING between the read and the router repaying it, so `debtToRepay` deliberately EXCEEDS what the position owes. The over-buy is the projected accrual over the inclusion window plus a small safety margin, and a trailing `SWEEP` returns whatever the buffer did not need. A close therefore reports `debtRepaid` (the debt itself) and `collateralReturned`, and reports NO leverage, liquidation price or health factor, because the position it describes will not exist. A position whose collateral cannot cover buying its debt back within the slippage-padded cap is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_CLOSE_UNFUNDABLE` rather than answered with a negative payout.

A composite populates MORE than one operation, in the order they execute, and the equity side sits on opposite ends depending on which way it moves. A supply goes FIRST, because it strictly lowers LTV, so the borrow that follows is the only step raising it. A withdrawal goes LAST, matching what the router does. Both withdraw composites currently pay out ONLY in the position's collateral token, for the same reason the bare `withdrawEquity` does.

Which direction an action swaps in is decided by the SOLVE, not by the key. A target above what the position already holds buys collateral with borrowed funds and emits `INCREASE_POSITION` with `collateralToBuy` and `maxDebtIn`; a target below it sells collateral to repay debt and emits `DECREASE_POSITION` with `debtToRepay` and `maxCollateralIn`. `addEquityAndDecreaseLeverage` does BOTH depending on the numbers: deleveraging does not imply selling, it implies the equity grew faster than the size, so a modest target still buys while an aggressive one sells. The bound is always on the side the router gives up.

All six leverage-target keys (`increaseLeverage`, `decreaseLeverage` and the four equity composites) price whichever leg the solve's sign calls for, through the same v4 quoter: a target the position reaches by buying prices a leverage leg, and one it can only reach by selling prices a deleverage leg. So `addEquityAndDecreaseLeverage` normally still BUYS, and a target low enough to need a sale is priced as a `DECREASE_POSITION` rather than refused. What IS refused is a target that leaves the position exactly where it is with no equity moving, which is a `MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH` rather than an empty operation.

`increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage` hold EQUITY and move only the debt, which is the mirror of the equity keys. Both price a leverage-side leg, so both require the top-level `slippageTolerance`, and both forbid the wallet rail entirely: nothing crosses the wallet boundary, so neither serves a `funding` block. The key is an ASSERTION about which way leverage moves, checked before the leverage leg is priced (on the two add composites the wallet-side funding swap is priced first, since the target is measured against the equity it actually delivers, so a funding refusal precedes an intent mismatch there): a target on the wrong side of the position's current leverage is refused with `MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH` naming the key that fits (an `increaseLeverage` aimed below current leverage names `decreaseLeverage`, and the composites are corrected on their leverage axis only), while a target exactly at the current leverage satisfies either key. A target past the buffered LTV ceiling is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX`. A target the position reaches by buying is held to the borrow-side ceiling `GET /margin/markets` serves as `maxLeverage`, read for the position's own account; one it reaches by selling is held to the liquidation LTV less the cliff buffer alone, because the venue checks no LTV on a repay, so a position that drifted past the borrow-side ceiling can still step down. Both withdraw composites are the exception: they are held to the withdrawal ceiling below whichever way they swap, since a repay in the same plan does not relax the ceiling a withdrawal is held to.

The two equity keys hold size, so they borrow nothing, swap nothing on the leverage side and move no debt: their whole effect is on the collateral, which makes leverage fall on an add and rise on a withdrawal. Neither serves an `effectivePrice`, because there is no swap for one to describe, and their single operation is `ADD_COLLATERAL` or `WITHDRAW`.

`withdrawEquity` currently pays out ONLY in the position's collateral token: its `walletToken` must equal that collateral, and any other value is refused with `MARGIN_FUNDING_SWAP_UNSUPPORTED`, because the swap that would sell the proceeds is not priced yet. A withdrawal is also held under the lower of the venue's liquidation threshold less the LTV cliff buffer and the LTV the venue lends at, so a request that would land the position on the edge is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX` even when it is under the venue's own limit.

MarginBadRequest400.description:
The request was refused before anything was priced. `errorCode` is `RequestValidationError` when the body or query failed schema validation, which on `POST /margin/quote` includes sending no action key or more than one, an `open` without a `marketId` that is 0x-prefixed 32-byte hex, a wallet block or `slippageTolerance` on a key that forbids it, a `leverageTarget` at or below 1, an `autoSlippage` or a missing `swapConfig.slippageTolerance`, a `slippageTolerance` or `swapConfig.slippageTolerance` above 5, an `amount` that is zero, has leading zeros or exceeds 2^128 - 1, and a `positionId` with leading zeros or above 2^256 - 1; it is `BadRequest` when the request parsed but the margin domain refused it, with the margin code in `detail`, optionally followed by `: ` and a corrective hint.

On `POST /margin/quote` the codes are: `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_SUPPORTED`, the chain has no margin configuration (or no v4 quoter), or the position's venue is not configured (a market the service does not serve is not this code: it is a 422 `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_FOUND` on `open` and `MARGIN_POSITION_NOT_FOUND` on the manage keys); `MARGIN_MARKET_MISMATCH`, on `open`, the market `open.marketId` names is not the request's pair on the side `direction` puts it: on a `LONG` its collateral must be `exposureToken` and its debt `counterToken`, on a `SHORT` the reverse; `MARGIN_MIRRORED_READING`, on `open`, `direction` reads the market in a way `GET /margin/markets` does not list it: a USD stablecoin as the exposure against a volatile token (a `SHORT` of USDT against WBTC is the WBTC long, a `LONG` of USDC against WETH the WETH short), or the `SHORT` of a stablecoin against a stablecoin; against a volatile token send the listed row instead, the volatile token as `exposureToken` and the direction flipped, and a stablecoin against a stablecoin is served only as the `LONG` of its collateral; `MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH`, the action key contradicts the numbers. A leverage target on the wrong side of the position's current leverage names the key to send instead on its leverage axis only (`MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH: decreaseLeverage` for an `increaseLeverage` aimed below current leverage, and likewise for the composites), a withdrawal of every last unit of collateral from a position that still owes debt, or a withdraw composite taking out all of the equity, names `close`, and a target that moves nothing, or an `open` whose target buys no collateral at all, carries no suffix; `MARGIN_POSITION_NOT_FOUND`, no live position with that `positionId` for this `swapper` on this market, or the account holds collateral on more than one venue's market for the pair and neither debt nor the owner's stored `ACTIVE` position settles which one is the position (anyone can supply collateral to an account but only the account can borrow, so a single market carrying debt is served first, then the single one the stored position names, a stored position recording more collateral than its market now holds naming none); `MARGIN_FUNDING_SWAP_UNSUPPORTED`, `walletChainId` differs from `positionChainId` on a pay-out key, or a pay-out key (`close`, `withdrawEquity` and the withdraw composites) named a `walletToken` other than the position's collateral, with the suffix `pays out in <collateral address>` naming the token to send as `walletToken` instead; `MARGIN_SLIPPAGE_TOLERANCE_REQUIRED`, a leg that swaps reached pricing without an explicit tolerance, a backstop behind the schema, which requires both; `MARGIN_DUST_DEBT`, on the leverage-target keys, the decrease would leave the position owing more than zero but under 10,000 raw units of its debt token, too little for any venue mark to read; raise `leverageTarget`, or `close`; `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX` on `open` only, the market `open.marketId` names has a buffered leverage ceiling below `leverageTarget`, so lowering it is the fix (a market lending nothing against the collateral is a 422 `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE` instead, since no target is servable) (on the manage keys the same code is a 422, because the position's own state decides it).

On `GET /margin/markets` the codes are: `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_SUPPORTED`, the chain has no margin configuration; `MARGIN_INVALID_CURSOR`, a `cursor` that does not decode, refused rather than restarting at page one. An unrecognised `venues` value is a `RequestValidationError`.

On `GET /margin/positions` the codes are: `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_SUPPORTED`, the chain has no margin configuration; `MARGIN_INVALID_CURSOR`, a `cursor` that is base64 but does not decode. `statuses` that mix `ACTIVE` with a finished status, name a status twice, are empty or fall outside the enum, and the retired `status` parameter, are a `RequestValidationError`.

On `GET /margin/assets` the code is `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_SUPPORTED`, the chain has no margin configuration. A missing or non-numeric `chainId`, or any query key besides `chainId`, is a `RequestValidationError`.

TransactionReadUnavailable503.description: Margin plans only: the transaction, its receipt or its trace could not be read from the chain, and the proof was not recorded. `errorCode` is `ServiceUnavailable` and `detail` is `Transaction could not be read from the chain`. Retryable with the same proof. With `detail` `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE`, the update would serve the `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step of an open but could not read the market or the wallet's sub-accounts: the update's other step progress was saved, and the margin step stays `NOT_READY` for `GET /plan/{planId}` and later updates to retry.

MarginUnavailable503.description: A venue's on-chain state could not be read, or a read that prices funding from another chain failed. `errorCode` is `ServiceUnavailable` and `detail` is `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE` unless named below. Retryable. On `POST /margin/quote` with funding from another chain, `MARGIN_FUNDING_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE` when a routing or bridge dependency timed out pricing the funding route, and `MARGIN_POSITION_CHAIN_READ_UNAVAILABLE` when the swapper's code on the position's chain, which decides whether Across pays a wrapped-native collateral as native and whether the wallet is a contract that must already permit the margin router, could not be read, or when a contract wallet's Permit2 allowance for the margin router could not be read. On `POST /margin/quote`: a market snapshot, a token's decimals, a quoter, pool-depth or v2 reserves read that routes and prices a leverage leg (an RPC failure, not a revert for want of a pool), the v4 PoolManager's balance of the leverage swap's input token or, on `close`, the borrow rate that sizes the accrual buffer was unavailable, or a venue's oracle answered a zero mark, so the mark and the risk numbers cannot be derived; an unavailable gas oracle does NOT produce this, since `gasEstimate` is indicative and is simply omitted. On `POST /margin/quote` with a swap from `walletToken` on the position's chain, `MARGIN_POSITION_CHAIN_READ_UNAVAILABLE` when the swapper's allowance of `walletToken` to Permit2, or its Permit2 allowance to the Universal Router, which decide the funding's approval steps, could not be read. On `GET /margin/markets`: a market-discovery read (router or adapter multicall) failed. On `POST /plan` with a `marginQuote`, a read that re-derives the margin step was unavailable, the PoolManager's balance included, and the plan was not created; with funding from another chain, `MARGIN_POSITION_CHAIN_READ_UNAVAILABLE` when the swapper's code on the position's chain, or a contract wallet's Permit2 allowance for the margin router, could not be read, and `MARGIN_FUNDING_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE` when the bridge's re-price timed out; `MARGIN_PLAN_CREATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` when building the plan took longer than the server allows before saving it, so neither the plan nor its position id reservation was written. On the `POST /margin/quote` keys that name a `positionId`, this also answers when a venue that could hold the position reverted its position read and no market holding collateral for the account carries debt or is named by the owner's stored `ACTIVE` position, since the unreadable venue may hold the position beside another's donated collateral, or when the account holds collateral on more than one venue's market with no single one carrying debt and the stored positions that would settle it could not be read; a venue's revert never blocks a position that carries debt on another venue or that the owner's stored `ACTIVE` position names. On `GET /margin/positions`: an account or position probe failed at the RPC, a venue reverted its position read and no other venue holds a position, or a token's decimals could not be read; a venue whose position read reverts is otherwise skipped. On `GET /margin/assets`: the shared catalogue's market-discovery read or a venue's support-gate multicall failed, or discovery returned no markets.

longOpenMorpho.description: The shape is authoritative; the numbers are illustrative. Equity is paid in WETH, which is the collateral token for a long, so no wallet-side swap was priced and `funding` is absent. `collateralToBuy` is 2 WETH: 1 WETH of equity at 3x leaves 2 WETH to buy with borrowed USDC, and `maxDebtIn` is the expected USDC spend padded up by the 0.5% leverage-leg tolerance. `display` describes the position that padded spend leaves, so its leverage reads above the 3x that `execution.leverageTarget` echoes. `positionId` and `legs[].subId` are absent because an open has no position yet; `gasEstimate` is omitted here.

MarginDisabled403.description: Margin trading is switched off in this environment: `detail` is `MARGIN_TRADING_DISABLED` and `errorCode` is `Forbidden`. The kill switch is read per request and checked before any margin logic runs, so nothing about the request is wrong and nothing in it can be changed to get through. Production and staging default closed; dev, preview and local default open.

MarginUnprocessable422.description: The request is well formed but cannot be priced as asked. `errorCode` is `UnprocessableEntity` and `detail` is the margin code with no suffix: `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_FOUND`, on `open`, `open.marketId` names no market `GET /margin/markets` lists on `positionChainId`, an id taken on another chain included; markets are listed and delisted over time, so take a fresh id from `GET /margin/markets`; `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE`, on `open`, the market `open.marketId` names is closed to new positions, or its venue cannot hold it at all (it no longer supports the market, has no oracle the service can mark against, or lends nothing against the collateral, as an Aave reserve frozen by zeroing its LTV), or refuses the open at the block read: its collateral or debt reserve paused, frozen or no longer active, borrowing disabled on the debt, the Aave v4 hub halting the spoke on either asset, or too little room under the collateral's Aave v3 supply cap or Aave v4 hub add cap for the equity and the `collateralToBuy` the open is served, as `POST /plan` counts it, either cap's room held back by the interest the collateral's borrowers can accrue in the 1,200 s after plan create (the 900 s its margin step has to be served in, then the 300 s its call stays sendable) and one more 12 s block, and on Aave v3 also since the reserve last updated (a plan funded from another chain can be served later than that, and its caps are not checked again when the funds land); the open is never moved to another market or venue, and a market with room for the equity but not the size asked is sized and refused only if it lacks room for what it is served; all of which a later block may change, and on a manage key, the service no longer serves the position's market on its venue, which refuses exits too (a `close` then answers 400 `MARGIN_POSITION_NOT_FOUND`, since positions are only read on served markets), or, on a key that supplies collateral or borrows, its venue refuses that supply or borrow the same way (a frozen reserve still serves `decreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquity` and `close`), and on any key a token of the pair answers like no ERC20 (no code, or no `decimals()`); `MARGIN_VENUE_WITHDRAWALS_UNAVAILABLE`, the venue will not let the collateral out at the block read: on `close`, on `decreaseLeverage` and a composite that sells or withdraws, and on `withdrawEquity`, the collateral reserve is paused or no longer active (or, on Aave v4, the hub halts the spoke), the debt reserve an exit repays into is paused or no longer active (or halted on the Aave v4 hub), or the venue holds less of the collateral unlent than the action can take out, a sale counted at its `maxCollateralIn` together with any withdrawal beside it, as `POST /plan` counts it; a frozen reserve still pays out, so it is not refused, and the same request may be served once the venue resumes; `MARGIN_INSUFFICIENT_BORROW_LIQUIDITY`, on `open`, the market's venue would have to lend more than it can, Aave v4 included, whose hub reports what it can lend and whose spoke draw cap bounds it (the manage keys do not check lendable balance); `MARGIN_CROSS_CHAIN_FUNDING_ROUTE_UNSUPPORTED`, on a pay-in funded from another chain, `walletChainId` is not a chain Across bridges from, no bridge corridor reaches the collateral, or the priced route starts with a step the funding floor cannot be derived from; a step of that route no quoter answers is `MARGIN_SWAP_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`, as is a floor that rounds to zero, and a step past the chained price impact cap is `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT`; `MARGIN_CROSS_CHAIN_CONTRACT_WALLET_PERMIT_UNSUPPORTED`, on a pay-in funded from another chain, the swapper's wallet on the position's chain is a contract (code that is not an EIP-7702 delegation) holding no Permit2 allowance for the margin router on the collateral that covers the equity, `funding.output.minimumAmount`, past the outer deadline a plan created now would get (3,600 s for the funds to land, then 1,800 s). A permit it signed would be an EIP-1271 signature, which the permit step cannot verify, so the bridged funds would land and no position would open. The quote cannot see how the plan will be sent, so such a wallet is refused even when its `POST /plan` `walletExecutionContext` is EIP-5792 and would batch an on-chain Permit2 approval of the router into the margin step instead, and `POST /plan` refuses it the same way. Only this quote's equity is checked, and each margin step spends an allowance below the maximum down, so a wallet with several such plans in flight needs an allowance covering all of them; grant the margin router that Permit2 allowance on the position's chain first, or fund from the position's chain. A wallet with no code or an EIP-7702 delegation signs as its EOA and is never refused this way; `MARGIN_SWAP_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`, a swap leg cannot be priced or bounded: no route for the wallet-side swap, a wallet-side swap whose floor at `swapConfig.slippageTolerance` rounds to zero, no route to price the leverage leg through (the leg routes over the chain's vetted v2, v3 and v4 pools, directly or through one hub token, one protocol per route, and a route whose gas limit, sized from its own quote at this size, would pass the 2,000,000 cap is not offered), a leverage swap wider than the router's uint128 amount, or a fill so small that its slippage bound rounds to zero, which the router refuses outright; `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT`, the leverage leg would fill more than 150bps above the chosen route's own marginal price, measured against the route rather than against any oracle, and on leverage that cost is an instant drawdown multiplied by the leverage, so a smaller size may be served; `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT_UNMEASURABLE`, that impact cannot be measured because the route will not price the small reference fill it is measured against, which a smaller size does not fix. Neither is raised on `close`, where refusing would leave the caller unable to exit; `MARGIN_SWAP_ALL_IN_COST`, on a leverage leg that buys or sells, the expected fill would cost more than 300bps over the venue's mark, the price the position is valued at, so a route's fees and impact together cannot cost more than that against the oracle at the quoted fill; the slippage tolerance the swap's bound allows (`maxDebtIn`, `maxCollateralIn`) is on top of it; also never raised on `close`; `MARGIN_POOL_MANAGER_INVENTORY`, the router flash-borrows the leverage swap's input bound (`maxDebtIn`, or `maxCollateralIn` on a sale and on `close`) from the Uniswap v4 PoolManager, and the PoolManager holds less of the input token than that bound plus 10% headroom, the room its balance has to move before the transaction lands; `close` keeps no headroom and is refused only when the balance is under the bound itself, when the transaction would revert on chain, since refusing earlier would leave the caller unable to exit; on `open` and on the keys that buy, also refused when the PoolManager holds less of the collateral than closing the resulting position would flash-borrow, its whole debt valued at the venue's mark plus the slippage tolerance, so no position is opened that cannot be closed in one transaction; a smaller size may still be served, and the PoolManager's balance moves block to block; `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX` on the manage keys, the position AFTER the action would sit at or past the venue's buffered LTV ceiling, including a `withdrawEquity` that walks it there (on `open` the same code is a 400 when the target itself is past the market's ceiling, since lowering `leverageTarget` is the fix), and on the composite keys that buy, the debt the leverage swap may spend at its slippage bound, valued at the venue's mark, would land the position at or past that ceiling even though the target is under it (`open` and `increaseLeverage` instead buy the most that clears it, and are refused only when no buy does); `MARGIN_POSITION_UNDERWATER`, on the six leverage-target keys, the venue reports the position's debt at or above its collateral value, so there is no equity for a leverage target to multiply; `MARGIN_CLOSE_UNFUNDABLE`, on `close` the collateral the position holds cannot cover buying its debt back within the slippage-padded cap, so the exit cannot be funded from the position itself and is refused rather than reported as a negative payout.

CreatePlanRateLimited429.description: Rate limited. `errorCode` `Ratelimited`: the caller exceeded its request rate. `errorCode` `TooManyRequests` with `detail` `MARGIN_SUBID_CLAIMS_PER_OWNER_EXCEEDED`: on a margin open, the calling session already holds 4 outstanding sub-account claims on this wallet, one for each open plan it created that is neither `COMPLETED` nor `FAILED` and whose open has not landed on chain, or 8 live claims on it whose plans are not `COMPLETED`, `FAILED` ones included. A plan takes its claim when its `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step is served: at `POST /plan` when that step is the plan's first, otherwise once every step before it has completed. The claim lapses 300 seconds after that call's deadline, which is 300 seconds after it was served. It stops counting toward the 4 once its plan is `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`, toward the 8 once its plan is `COMPLETED`, and toward both limits once its open lands on chain. Retry after any of these; executing a pending plan, rather than creating another, avoids it. `POST /plan` checks these limits without taking a claim. When they refuse the claim as the margin step is served, `PATCH /plan/{planId}` and `GET /plan/{planId}` answer 200 instead: the update's step progress is saved, the margin step stays `NOT_READY` with no transaction, and later reads and updates retry serving it until the step's 15 minutes pass.

ReservationContended409.description: A margin open could not claim a sub-account. Neither case is a server fault or needs operator action. `errorCode` `ReservationContendedError`: the subId this plan was allocated was claimed by another plan between the allocation read and the write, and nothing was written; retrying the same request allocates the next free subId. `errorCode` `Conflict` with `detail` `MARGIN_SUBID_UNAVAILABLE`: no sub-account is free for this wallet, since each one the service would hand out already holds a position or is claimed by another open plan. A claim lapses 300 seconds after its margin call's deadline, which is 300 seconds after the call was served, so retry after that. On `POST /plan` nothing was persisted. Neither answers `PATCH /plan/{planId}` or `GET /plan/{planId}`: when the margin step cannot claim a sub-account as it is served, they answer 200 with the update's step progress saved and the margin step left `NOT_READY` with no transaction, and later reads and updates retry serving it.

PlanForbidden403.description: The plan exists but cannot be served to this caller. Either it was created by another caller: `errorCode` is `ForbiddenError` and `detail` is `Caller is not the owner of this plan`, since only the caller that created a plan (the same session or API key) can read, refresh or update it. Or it is a margin plan and margin trading is switched off in this environment: `errorCode` is `Forbidden` and `detail` is `MARGIN_TRADING_DISABLED`, as on `POST /margin/quote` and `POST /plan`. The switch is read per request, so while it is off a margin plan is neither served, refreshed nor updated, whatever its status, and none of its calldata is returned. A transaction already sent from it is recorded by re-sending its PATCH once the switch reopens, unless the plan has expired by then. Other plans never read the switch.

StalePlan409.description: A concurrent request saved a newer version of the plan between this update's read and its write, so nothing from this request was saved: `errorCode` is `StalePlanError`. Re-GET the plan and PATCH again if the step still needs the proof; re-sending a proof the step already records is accepted without change. On a margin open, an update whose `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step cannot claim a sub-account as it is served answers 200, not 409: the update's step progress is saved, the margin step stays `NOT_READY` with no transaction, and `GET /plan/{planId}` and later updates retry serving it.

senderWalletAddress.description: The wallet address which will be used to send the token.

receiverWalletAddress.description: (optional) The wallet address which will receive the output of the swap. If not provided, the output is returned to the `swapper`.

contractAddress.description: The address of a contract which will be used to facilitate the swap.

cosignerAddress.description: The address of a cosigner who will run the auction and ensure the best executable price within the given parameters. Currently the cosigner is always Uniswap Labs.

inputToken.description: The token which will be sent, specified by its token address. For a list of supported tokens, see the [FAQ](https://api-docs.uniswap.org/guides/faqs).

outputToken.description: The token which will be received, specified by its token address. For a list of supported tokens, see the [FAQ](https://api-docs.uniswap.org/guides/faqs).

tokenAmount.description: The quantity of tokens denominated in the token's base units. (For example, for an ERC20 token one token is 1x10^18 base units. For one USDC token one token is 1x10^6 base units.) This value must be greater than 0.

generatePermitAsTransaction.description: Indicates whether you want to receive a permit2 transaction to sign and submit onchain, or a permit message to sign. When set to `true`, the quote response returns the Permit2 as a calldata which the user signs and broadcasts. When set to `false` (the default), the quote response returns the Permit2 as a message which the user signs but does not need to broadcast. When using a 7702-delegated wallet, set this field to `true`. Except for this scenario, it is recommended that this field is set to false. Note that a Permit2 calldata (e.g. `true`), will provide indefinite permission for Permit2 to spend a token, in contrast to a Permit2 message (e.g. `false`) which is only valid for 30 days. Further, a Permit2 calldata (e.g. `true`) requires the user to pay gas to submit the transaction, whereas the Permit2 message (e.g. `false` ) does not require the user to submit a transaction and requires no gas.

slippageTolerance.description:
The slippage tolerance as a percentage up to a maximum of two decimal places, between 0 and 100 (a value outside that range is rejected). This is the maximum acceptable output loss as a percentage: for exact-input trades, the minimum received is expectedOut × (1 - slippageTolerance); for exact-output trades, the maximum input is expectedIn × (1 + slippageTolerance).

When submitting a quote, note that slippage tolerance works differently in UniswapX swaps where it does not set a limit on the Spread in an order. See [here](https://api-docs.uniswap.org/guides/faqs#why-do-uniswapx-quotes-have-more-slippage-than-the-tolerance-i-set) for more information.

Note that if the trade type is `EXACT_INPUT`, then the slippage is in terms of the output token. If the trade type is `EXACT_OUTPUT`, then the slippage is in terms of the input token.

When submitting a request, `slippageTolerance` may not be set when `autoSlippage` is defined. One of `slippageTolerance` or `autoSlippage` must be defined.

txHash.description: On-chain transaction hash. Present for transaction queries and for userOperation queries once the userOp has been included on-chain.

userOpHash.description: ERC-4337 userOperation hash. Present only when the row corresponds to a userOperation query.

hashType.description: Identifies whether the row was resolved from a transaction hash or a userOperation hash. Omitted on transaction rows; absence is equivalent to `TX`.

paymaster.description: Paymaster address from the userOperation receipt. Present only for userOperation queries when the receipt is available and a paymaster was used.

fillTxHash.description: The destination-chain transaction that filled a bridge, once its bridge provider reports the fill. Absent for Across bridges, which carry `swapId` instead.

sponsorship.description: Present only when `swapper` is supplied and the transaction's gas fees were sponsored by Uniswap. Use this to display "Sponsored by Uniswap" in activity history.

version.description: Only present where it distinguishes deployments: contract release lines (e.g. UniversalRouter 2.0/2.1.2) and same-named contracts (Quoter V3 vs V4).

decimals.description: The number of decimals supported by the token. This number is used to convert token amounts to the token's common representation.

UniversalRouterVersion.description: Universal Router release line. isTokenApprovalApplicable.description: Whether an ERC-20 token approval is applicable to this swap's input. `true` when the routing pulls the input token via an allowance, so an approval may be required — verify (or orchestrate) it via `/check_approval`. `false` when no approval is ever needed for this route (e.g. native-currency input, wrap/unwrap, or a native-gas-token input paid as native value). Reflects the routing mechanism, not the swapper's current on-chain allowance. If absent, assume an approval is applicable.

swapTransaction.description: Ready-to-send swap transaction, returned for CLASSIC quotes when no permit signature needs to be embedded in the calldata. That's the case when the request used `x-permit2-disabled: true`, the swapper already holds a valid permit (`permitData` is `null`), or the permit was requested as a transaction (`generatePermitAsTransaction: true`). The returned calldata is built with default settings (`safetyMode: SAFE`, deadline 30 minutes ahead); use `/swap` to customize them. Not returned when `txFailureReasons` is populated; call `/swap` to build the calldata anyway. With `swapSource: "UNIVERSAL_ROUTER"` a failed simulation returns a 422 instead of a quote without calldata, except for `TRANSFER_FROM_FAILED` and `SLIPPAGE_TOO_LOW`, which still return calldata. `/swap` is unchanged for these quotes.

swapGasFee.description: The estimated gas fee for `swapTransaction`, equal to the `gasFee` that `/swap` would return without gas refresh. Only present when `swapTransaction` is present.

integratorFees.description: Optional integrator fees: up to 4 entries, on both UniswapX and classic (Universal Router) routes. Urgency.description: The urgency impacts the estimated gas price of the transaction. The higher the urgency, the higher the gas price, and the faster the transaction is likely to be selected from the mempool. Send the bare string form (e.g. `"normal"`) for the common case, or the object form `{ level, overrides }` to supply caller caps for `maxPriorityFeePerGas`, `maxFeePerGas`, and `gasLimit`.

maxFeePerGas.description: Maximum total fee per gas in wei (decimal string).

gasLimit.description: Gas limit cap (in gas units, decimal string).

Protocols.description: The protocols to use for the swap/order. If the `protocols` field is defined, then you can only set the `routingPreference` to `BEST_PRICE`. Note that the value `UNISWAPX` is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

HooksOptions.description: The hook options to use for V4 pool quotes. `V4_HOOKS_INCLUSIVE` will get quotes for V4 pools with or without hooks. `V4_HOOKS_ONLY` will only get quotes for V4 pools with hooks. `V4_NO_HOOKS` will only get quotes for V4 pools without hooks. errorCode.description: Cause of the no-quote response. QuoteAmountTooLowError: amount is below the minimum quotable size for the requested protocols. NoRouteFoundError: no route with sufficient liquidity exists for this pair. UnsupportedTokenError: one of the tokens is not routable. UnsupportedChainError: the chain is not supported for this operation. UniswapXNotSupportedOnChainError: the requested UniswapX protocol is not available on this chain. UpstreamTimeoutError: a routing dependency timed out; the request may succeed on retry. ResourceNotFound: the failure could not be classified. Treat unrecognized values like ResourceNotFound.

decayStartTime.description: The unix timestamp at which the order will be eligible to be filled by alternate fillers at a lower price. Noted that the fill amount will not be lower than the output `endAmount`.

OrderStatus.description:
The status of the order. Note that all of these are final states with the exception of Open, meaning that no further state changes will occur. 
 Open - order is not yet filled by a filler.
 Expired - order has expired without being filled and is no longer fillable.
 Error - a catchall for other final states which are not otherwise specified, where the order will not be filled.
 Cancelled - order is cancelled. Note that to cancel an order, a new order must be placed with the same nonce as the prior open order and it must be placed within the same block as the original order.
 Filled - order is filled.
 Insufficient-funds - the swapper (you) do not have enough funds for the order to be completed and the order is cancelled and will not be filled.
 Unverified - order has not been verified yet.

requestedAssets.description: Requested underlying asset amount for EXACT_ASSETS withdraw intents.

MarginPlanIntent.description:
Names the margin position a plan acts on. Present only on a margin plan, so its absence is how a client tells one from a swap plan. Everything the router needs -- adapter, universal router, pool key, bounds, deadline -- stays server-side. `marketKey` is display-only: resolve the market from `collateralToken`, `debtToken` and `venue` rather than by parsing it.

On a margin plan the `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step's `tokenInAmount` is the collateral pulled from the wallet. Its `tokenOutAmount`, and the plan's `expectedOutput`, are what the plan pays the wallet on the keys that pay out (`withdrawEquity`, the two withdraw composites, and `close`, where it is the floor of the collateral returned), and the collateral committed to the position on every other key. Once the step's transaction is proved, its `tokenOutAmount` on a key that pays out is the collateral that transaction paid the wallet, and on every other key it stays the committed collateral. The plan grants the margin router a Permit2 allowance, as an `APPROVAL_PERMIT` step or, for a wallet that batches, a Permit2 approval inside the batched `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step, unless the wallet's allowance to it covers the `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step's `tokenInAmount` and outlasts the plan's execute deadline.

subId.description: The sub-account the position lives in. On an open it is `""` until the `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step is `AWAITING_ACTION`, then the sub-account the server reserved for it when it built that call.

AggregatedOutput.description: An array of all outputs of the proposed transaction. This includes the swap as well as any fees collected by the API integrator. This does not include pool fees when routing is through a Uniswap Protocol pool.

fee.description: Set to INTEGRATOR when this output is an integrator fee (as specified by the `integratorFees` array in the /quote request); omitted for the core output of the swap. One INTEGRATOR output is returned per fee recipient, in the order the recipients were requested, and their amounts sum to the amount deducted from the core output.

v4BatchPermitData.description: Batch permit data for V4 positions, if applicable.

quote.description: The `BRIDGE` quote from `/quote`, passed as `/swap` takes it. The approval then goes to the contract that quote's deposit pulls from (the Across SpokePool, or Relay's depository or approval proxy) instead of the inferred spender. A provider quote must be one this API issued, unaltered and unexpired, and the quote's ERC-20 input must be `token` on `chainId`.

tokens.description: Tokens to check permissions for. Maximum of 2 per request.

isPermissioned.description: Whether the token requires a permissioned adapter to trade.

isAllowlisted.description: Only provided when isPermissioned is true. Indicates whether the wallet is allowed to swap this token.

adapterTokenAddress.description: Address of the permissioned adapter token to use in place of the underlying token. Always provided when isPermissioned is true.

kycUrl.description: URL the wallet holder must visit to complete KYC and become allowlisted. Always provided when isAllowlisted is false.

issuer.description: KYC provider display name (e.g. "Superstate"). Always provided when isPermissioned is true.

gasUseEstimate.description: The estimated gas use. It does NOT include the additional gas for token approvals.

txFailureReasons.description: The reason(s) why the transaction failed during simulation.

priceImpact.description: The impact the trade has on the market price of the pool, between 0-100 percent

swapSteps.description: Universal Router swap step sequence. Additive, opt-in via the `x-universal-router-swapsteps` header. When present, mirrors the inputs to `SwapRouter.encodeSwaps`. Only emitted when GuideStar wins the hybrid quoter race (`EXACT_INPUT` today; broader coverage once UniRoute's transformer ships).

routeCandidates.description: Top route candidates the router considered but did NOT serve (the served route and candidates proven unviable — simulation or trade-build failures — are excluded), best-first. Additive, opt-in via the `includeRouteCandidates` request flag; only populated for uniroute-backed quotes. May be short or empty when the route cache limits the candidate pool.

priceDifference.description: The expected value lost versus frictionless execution at current prices, as a percent between -100 and 100. Negative values indicate price improvement. For classic swaps this equals priceImpact, the pool-based impact reported by routing.

gasLimit.description: The minimum gas limit for the swap transaction, in gas units, as a positive decimal integer string. Only present when the route goes through a pool whose swap needs more gas available than it uses (for example, a hook that checks `gasleft()`). When the response includes `permitData`, it already includes the gas for that Permit2 permit; it does NOT include the gas for an ERC-20 approval transaction. Pass the quote back to `/swap` unchanged: the swap transaction's gas limit is at least this value. A quote whose `gasLimit` is not a positive decimal integer string is rejected with a 400 `RequestValidationError`.

RouteCandidate.description: A quoted route candidate with its whole-route (not per-hop) amounts.

routeString.description: The candidate route in string format.

quoteAmount.description: The whole-route quoted amount: output amount for EXACT_INPUT, required input amount for EXACT_OUTPUT. A quoter estimate — does not carry the simulation/portion corrections applied to the served quote.

quoteGasAdjusted.description: The gas-adjusted whole-route amount. Omitted when gas details are unavailable.

RouteGraph.description: Pool-level graph of the quoted route: one entry per pool hop, in swap direction. Omitted whenever it cannot be built completely (unresolvable token, shares that do not reconcile, a cycle), so it is either whole or absent.

pools.description: One entry per pool hop (edge). The same pool traversed in both directions appears twice.

RouteGraphPool.description: One pool hop of the quoted route, oriented in swap direction (input -> output) regardless of tradeType. `tokenIn`/`tokenOut` carry `address` and `symbol`; `decimals` is present only for the native currency and its wrapped token, so do not do amount math on it. A graph node is a token plus its visit index (`tokenInVisit`/`tokenOutVisit`), so a token the route passes through more than once appears as several nodes.

protocol.description: WRAP is the native <-> wrapped-native conversion step.

address.description: V2/V3 pool address (checksummed); V4 pool id (bytes32). Omitted for WRAP.

hooks.description: V4 hook contract. Omitted when the pool has no hook (never the zero address).

fee.description: Pool fee in the same units as V3PoolInRoute.fee (hundredths of a bip). Omitted for WRAP and for dynamic-fee pools.

tokenInVisit.description: Disambiguates repeated visits of the same token within the graph; absent means the first visit.

tokenOutVisit.description: Disambiguates repeated visits of the same token within the graph; absent means the first visit.

shareOfInputBps.description: Share of the trade's total input VALUE routed through this pool (USD-equivalent), in bps. Downstream pools trade a different token, so an amount share is undefined there; edges leaving the input token's first visit and edges entering the output token's first visit each sum to 10000 (within rounding), and flow is conserved at every other node.

usdIn.description: USD value entering the pool, as a decimal string. Omitted when no USD valuation is available.

usdOut.description: USD value leaving the pool, as a decimal string. Omitted when no USD valuation is available.

SwapStep.description: Universal Router swap step. Discriminated by the `type` field.

V4Action.description: V4 action. Discriminated by the `action` field.

priceDifference.description: The expected value lost versus frictionless execution at current prices, as a percent between -100 and 100. Negative values indicate price improvement. Always 0, since wraps and unwraps are 1:1.

decimals.description: The number of decimals supported by the token. This number is used to convert token amounts to the token's common representation.

V2Reserve.description: The remaining reserve of this token in the pool.

quotient.description: The quantity of this token remaining in the pool, specified in the base units of the token.

hooks.description: The address of the hook for the pool, if any. If the pool has no hook, this field will be the null address (e.g. 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000).

settleBeforeSwap.description: Set to true when the pool's hook needs the swap input in the PoolManager before the swap runs. The swap transaction then settles the input before the swap. Send the field back to /swap unchanged.

TransactionHash.description: The unique hash of the transaction.

RequestId.description: A unique ID for the request.

PermitAmount.description: For Uniswap Protocols (v2, v3, v4) swaps, specify the input token spend allowance (e.g. quantity) to be set in the Permit2 permit. Applies to both the Permit2 message (`generatePermitAsTransaction: false`) and the Permit2 approval transaction (`generatePermitAsTransaction: true`). `FULL` can be used to specify an unlimited token quantity, and may prevent the wallet from needing to sign another permit for the same token in the future. `EXACT` bounds the allowance to the most the swap may spend: the input amount for exact-input trades, and the quoted input amount plus slippage tolerance for exact-output trades. bips.description: Fee amount in basis points (1 bip = 0.01%). Must be greater than 0 and at most 500.

recipient.description: Ethereum address that receives the fee.

When set to `PRICE`, quotes optimize for tighter spreads at lower fill rates. AutoSlippage.description:
