marginQuote.description:
A margin quote echoed back verbatim, in place of `quote`. Exactly one of the two is accepted. Decoded strictly: an unknown field, an unrecognised enum string, a wrongly typed value, or a `slippageTolerance` or `funding.slippageTolerance` with more than two decimal places is a 400 `RequestValidationError`. Every bound and the route are re-derived from the venue and the chain's pools at plan create, and a re-derived `maxDebtIn` or `maxCollateralIn` is never looser than the one echoed, since that is the bound the caller agreed to.

Refused with a 400 `MARGIN_MIRRORED_READING`: an `open` whose `direction`, `exposureToken` and `counterToken` read its market as one `GET /margin/markets` does not list, as `POST /margin/quote` refuses it. Refused with a 400 `MARGIN_PLAN_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED`: a `legs[].subId` on `open`, which the service allocates; a `legs[].marketId` missing on `open`, present on any other key, or not 0x-prefixed 32-byte hex; an amount or `subId` that is not a non-negative integer string in range; a `funding` block without its `slippageTolerance`. Refused with a 422: `MARGIN_PRICE_DRIFT`, the leverage leg now costs more than the echoed `maxDebtIn` (or sells more than the echoed `maxCollateralIn`), so re-quote; `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT`, the leverage leg now crosses the quote's 150bps ceiling; `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT_UNMEASURABLE`, its impact can no longer be measured; `MARGIN_SWAP_ALL_IN_COST`, the re-derived leverage leg's expected fill now costs more than 300bps over the venue's mark; `MARGIN_POOL_MANAGER_INVENTORY`, the v4 PoolManager no longer holds the re-derived input bound of the token the router flash-borrows plus 10% headroom (the bound alone on a `close`), or on a buy no longer holds the collateral a close of the resulting position would flash-borrow; when `PATCH /plan/{planId}` rebuilds the margin step it requires only the bound itself, with no headroom, since the funding swap may already have run, and when the PoolManager holds less than that it answers 200 with the step left unbuilt in `NOT_READY` rather than serving fresh calldata; `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE`, the service no longer serves the market on the venue, or its state now refuses the supply or borrow the plan makes, as `POST /margin/quote` refuses it: a paused, frozen or inactive reserve, borrowing disabled on the debt, an Aave v4 hub halt, or too little room under the supply or add cap for the equity and the bought collateral the plan supplies, either cap's room held back by the interest the collateral's borrowers can accrue in the 1,200 s after plan create (the 900 s its margin step has to be served in, then the 300 s its call stays sendable) and one more block, and on Aave v3 also since the reserve last updated (a plan funded from another chain can be served later than that, and its caps are not checked again when the funds land); `MARGIN_VENUE_WITHDRAWALS_UNAVAILABLE`, on a `close`, a decrease or a withdrawal, the venue now will not let the collateral out or take the repay, as `POST /margin/quote` refuses it, with a decrease counted at its echoed `maxCollateralIn` together with any withdrawal beside it; `MARGIN_POSITION_CHANGED`, on a decrease, the position now owes less than the echoed `debtToRepay`, as after a liquidation since the quote, so re-quote. A `close` is never refused for impact, but it is refused with the 422 `MARGIN_PRICE_DRIFT` when its re-priced fill now sells more than the echoed `maxCollateralIn`, since the router would revert it. A 503 `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE`, including when the PoolManager balance or the venue's state cannot be read, means the plan was not created. On an `open`, a 409 `MARGIN_SUBID_UNAVAILABLE` means no sub-account is free for the wallet, and a 429 `MARGIN_SUBID_CLAIMS_PER_OWNER_EXCEEDED` means the calling session already holds 4 outstanding sub-account claims on it, or 8 live ones whose plans are not `COMPLETED`; neither creates a plan. These are checked at plan create without taking a claim: the sub-account is reserved, and the margin call built with a deadline 300 s out, when the `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step is served, at plan create when it is the plan's first step and otherwise once every step before it has completed; when the same refusals meet that later serve, `PATCH /plan/{planId}` and `GET /plan/{planId}` answer 200 with the step left `NOT_READY` for a later update to serve.

The wallet-side funding swap runs at `funding.slippageTolerance`, the tolerance its floor was derived at, and routes over V2, V3 and V4 pools without hooks, never UniswapX. When the swap re-quoted at plan create no longer floors at the equity, it is rebuilt at the narrower tolerance whose floor covers it, which its step's `slippage` reports, but never below half of `funding.slippageTolerance`: with less headroom over the equity than that, or an expected output below it, the plan is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_FUNDING_BELOW_EQUITY`, so re-quote. `PATCH /plan/{planId}` and a `forceRefresh` read answer the same 422 when the funding swap they rebuild is expected to deliver less than the equity; a rebuild left with less headroom than that floor keeps the funding step already served. The `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step's `slippage` is the leverage leg's tolerance its bounds were derived at, and is absent on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which price no leverage swap. An `open` is planned on the market its `legs[0].marketId` names, the one the quote priced: an id naming no market `GET /margin/markets` lists on `positionChainId` is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_FOUND`, a market that is not the echo's pair on the side `direction` puts it, or not on the leg's `venue`, with a 400 `MARGIN_MARKET_MISMATCH`, and a market closed to new positions with a 422 `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE`. When the catalogue is served from the margin market index, an `open`, `increaseLeverage`, `addEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquity`, `withdrawEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquityAndDecreaseLeverage`, and any other leg that borrows or withdraws, also has its market re-read from the index, uncached, when the plan is created and again when `PATCH /plan/{planId}` or `GET /plan/{planId}` serves the margin step, which builds it then: a market the index does not report open is a 422 `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE` on create and fails the step on an update, and a read that fails or takes longer than 300 ms is a 503 `MARGIN_MARKET_READ_UNAVAILABLE` on create and leaves the step in `NOT_READY` on an update.

Funding from another chain, a `funding.tokenInChainId` other than `positionChainId`, is planned only on `open`, `addEquity` and the two add-equity composites; on any other key it is refused with a 400 `MARGIN_PLAN_OPERATION_UNSUPPORTED` (`: cross-chain funding`). A `funding.minBridgeOut` absent or other than `funding.output.minimumAmount` is the same 400 with `: invalid funding.minBridgeOut`. A `funding.tokenInChainId` Across does not bridge from, or a collateral no corridor from it reaches, is a 422 `MARGIN_CROSS_CHAIN_FUNDING_ROUTE_UNSUPPORTED`. The plan routes over Across alone: the optional swap on the source chain, the bridge, a `WRAP` on the position's chain when the collateral is the wrapped native token and the swapper's wallet there has no code or an EIP-7702 delegation (Across pays such a wallet native currency; a 503 `MARGIN_POSITION_CHAIN_READ_UNAVAILABLE` means that code could not be read), then the position chain's approvals and `MARGIN_EXECUTE`. A contract wallet there (code that is not an EIP-7702 delegation) is planned only while it holds a Permit2 allowance for the margin router on the collateral covering the equity past the plan's outer deadline, since a permit it signed would be an EIP-1271 signature the permit step cannot verify; otherwise the plan is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_CROSS_CHAIN_CONTRACT_WALLET_PERMIT_UNSUPPORTED` before anything is served, whatever its `walletExecutionContext`, EIP-5792 included, as on `POST /margin/quote`, and a 503 `MARGIN_POSITION_CHAIN_READ_UNAVAILABLE` means that allowance could not be read. Only this plan's equity is checked against that allowance, which each margin step spends down unless it is the maximum. The equity is `funding.output.minimumAmount`. At plan create the bridge is re-priced at the source swap's own minimum, or at `funding.input.amount` when the route starts with the bridge, and Across's output there below the equity, a relay fee that rose by more than the 10 bps `funding.minBridgeOut` holds back, is a 422 `MARGIN_FUNDING_BELOW_EQUITY` whether or not the creation guards are switched off; a re-price no bridge quote answers is a 422 `MARGIN_SWAP_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`, and one whose bridge timed out a 503 `MARGIN_FUNDING_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE`, as on `POST /margin/quote`. The Across deposit's output is the larger of the equity and Across's output for the amount deposited less those 10 bps, so the fill lands at least the equity and the relayer keeps the rest of its fee move; a `PATCH /plan/{planId}` or `forceRefresh` read that re-prices the bridge before it is sent and finds Across's output below the equity ends the plan `FAILED`, so re-quote. Once the bridge fills, the next `PATCH /plan/{planId}` or `forceRefresh` read rebuilds the steps after it once, from the amount that landed: a landing below the equity ends `MARGIN_EXECUTE` in `STEP_ERROR` and the plan `FAILED`, with the funds left in the wallet on the position's chain. The funds must land within 3,600 s of plan create: the Across deposit's `fillDeadline` is capped there, so a deposit still unfilled then expires, Across refunds it on the source chain, and the plan ends `FAILED`; a rebuild before the bridge that would leave the deposit less than 600 s to fill ends the plan `FAILED` the same way, with the funds left in the wallet on the source chain. The rebuild once the funds land gives `MARGIN_EXECUTE` 1,800 s from that update to be served, and never more than 1,800 s past the time the funds had to land by; its call, once served, is sendable for 300 s and never past that outer deadline; the plan ends `FAILED` if the step is not served, or its call not sent, by then.

steps.description: Array of steps with proofs to attach. Only steps being updated need to be included.

StepUpdate.description: Represents a single step update with proof. Note: orderId is not accepted in update requests; it is system-generated after receiving a signature.

stepIndex.description: The index of the step being updated (0-based).

proof.description: Proof of step completion. Must provide either txHash or signature. An APPROVAL_PERMIT step that asks for a signature is proved by a txHash only when the last Permit2 approve, permit or lockdown in that transaction for the swapper's allowance of the permit's token to its spender is an approve or permit of at least the step's tokenInAmount that has not expired: a successful transaction without one is refused (400), and one still pending when sent turns the step to `STEP_ERROR` once it mines without one. A step that already holds a proof refuses a different one (400), except on a margin plan: an IN_PROGRESS step sent as a transaction, and a STEP_ERROR MARGIN_EXECUTE step, accept another txHash, such as a wallet speed-up or a resend, and a STEP_ERROR MARGIN_EXECUTE step its stored txHash again, only once that transaction has mined from the swapper and ran the step's call. A transaction still pending, reverted, not found or running another call, such as a cancel, is refused (400) and the stored proof is kept, and so is any other txHash for an IN_PROGRESS step whose stored transaction already mined from the swapper and ran the step's call; re-sending the stored txHash of a STEP_ERROR step that still does not prove it returns the plan unchanged.

planId.description: A unique identifier for this execution plan.

steps.description: The sequential steps that need to be executed to complete the plan.

currentStepIndex.description: The index of the current step that needs to be executed (0-based). On a FAILED plan, the step that failed. On any other plan, a STEP_ERROR step before this index was superseded by the rebuild served after it; act on the step at this index, not on any STEP_ERROR step.

timeEstimateMs.description: Estimated time in milliseconds to complete the entire plan.

gasStrategies.description: Gas strategies used for the plan.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the plan was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the plan was last updated.

lastUserActionAt.description: Timestamp of the last user action on this plan.

stepIndex.description: The index of this step in the plan (0-based).

payload.description: The payload data for this step. The structure depends on the payloadType. On a `MARGIN_EXECUTE` step it is `{}` until the step is `AWAITING_ACTION`: the margin call is built, and an open's sub-account reserved, only once every step before it has completed, so a `NOT_READY` margin step carries no transaction or batched `calls` to send. Never send a `NOT_READY` step.

gasUseEstimate.description: The estimated units of gas this step will consume; the step's gasFee is priced from it.

gasLimit.description: The units of gas to send as this step's transaction gas limit. Carries headroom over gasUseEstimate, so the two are not interchangeable.

routingStepKey.description: An optional key identifying the routing strategy used for this step.

bridgeProvider.description: The vendor that built a bridge step's deposit transaction. Absent for Across bridge steps and for non-bridge steps.

PlanStepProof.description: Proof of execution for a plan step, provided after the step is completed.

signature.description: The signature for a message signing step.

orderId.description: The order ID for a gasless order step.

PlanStatus.description: The overall status of the plan execution. ACTIVE means the plan is ready to begin (all steps NOT_READY). AWAITING_ACTION means at least one step requires user action. IN_PROGRESS means at least one step is executing. COMPLETED means all steps have been successfully executed. FAILED means the plan cannot be completed; it is reported for a margin plan whose MARGIN_EXECUTE step is STEP_ERROR, and is final except that a PATCH whose mined transaction ran the MARGIN_EXECUTE call records the plan COMPLETED. A margin plan also ends FAILED, answered with a 200 rather than a 422, when the funding swap it re-quotes, after that swap reverted or on a forceRefresh, would no longer deliver the margin equity or the output the plan was consented at; a reverted funding swap keeps its proof, and the client re-quotes. A margin plan ends FAILED the same way when, after one of its steps reverted, the margin call it rebuilds is refused, as it is when the PoolManager no longer holds what the call swaps; the reverted step keeps its proof and the MARGIN_EXECUTE step reads STEP_ERROR. A margin plan funded from another chain also ends FAILED when its Across deposit expires unfilled, which Across refunds on the source chain, or when its MARGIN_EXECUTE step has not been sent within 1,800 s of the update that found the funds landed.

PlanStepStatus.description: The status of an individual step. NOT_READY means prerequisites are not met. AWAITING_ACTION means the step is ready for user action. IN_PROGRESS means the step is being executed. COMPLETE means the step finished successfully. STEP_ERROR means the step failed. An IN_PROGRESS step of a margin plan whose transaction can no longer be found stays IN_PROGRESS until 300 seconds past the plan's execute deadline, the deadline of its margin call once that call is served, and only then becomes STEP_ERROR. A step of a margin plan whose transaction could not be read from the chain (an RPC failure) stays IN_PROGRESS whatever the deadline. A margin plan's MARGIN_EXECUTE step must be ready within 15 minutes of POST /plan: it is served, its call built and an open's sub-account reserved, once every step before it has completed, and that call expires 5 minutes after it is served. A MARGIN_EXECUTE step still NOT_READY when the 15 minutes pass, or still AWAITING_ACTION with no proof when its call expires, becomes STEP_ERROR on the next PATCH /plan, or GET /plan, so the plan ends FAILED instead of serving a call that can only revert. A MARGIN_EXECUTE step in STEP_ERROR still accepts the proof of a call it served. A margin plan's funding swap keeps the 15-minute deadline, so the Universal Router refuses it once the MARGIN_EXECUTE step can no longer be served.

PlanStepMethod.description: The execution method for the step. SEND_TX is a standard transaction. SIGN_MSG is for signing a message (e.g., permit). SEND_CALLS is for batch transaction execution (EIP-5792).

buyFee.description: Token buy fee as a percent. 0 when no fee or unknown.

sellFee.description: Token sell fee as a percent. 0 when no fee or unknown.

address.description: The token's address in its chain's native format. Not limited to EVM 0x addresses: `sort=default` mirrors the hosted token list, which includes non-EVM entries (e.g. Solana base58 addresses).

chainId.description: The unique ID of the blockchain the entry lives on. Not limited to chains supported for trading: `sort=default` mirrors the hosted token list, which includes non-EVM chains (e.g. Solana).

decimals.description: The number of decimals supported by the token.

logoURI.description: URI of the token logo. Null when no logo is available.

MarginDirection.description: Which side of the pair the position is exposed to. `LONG` borrows the counter token and buys the exposure token, so collateral is the exposure token and debt is the counter token. `SHORT` borrows the exposure token and sells it for the counter token, so collateral is the counter token and debt is the exposure token. The market is always addressed in trader terms: a client never sends a collateral/debt pair and never reorders `exposureToken`/`counterToken` to mean short.

MarginMarketRow.description: One row per (exposureToken, counterToken, direction). A venue market is a (collateral, debt) pair, read as a long of its collateral and a short of its debt except that a USD stablecoin is never the exposure unless both legs are one (served as the LONG of its collateral), so a market with one or two stablecoin legs produces one row, and shorting a token is only ever expressible as a market whose debt it is. Carries no `oraclePrice`: a mark belongs to a VENUE's oracle and two venues on one market need not agree, so a row-level price is a number no venue necessarily quoted. Carries no `feeBps` either: a pool fee tier is not a cost, since a 5bps pool with thin liquidity fills worse than a 30bps pool with depth. `effectivePrice` on a quote answers that, carrying the fee and the impact together.

headlineVenue.description: The venue of the headline market, the one behind `maxLeverage`. Several `venueMarkets` entries can share it, so it does not name the market.

headlineMarketId.description: The `marketId` of the headline market, the one behind `maxLeverage`: always the `marketId` of one of the row's `venueMarkets` entries. A quote opens on the market its `open.marketId` names, which need not be this one.

venueMarkets.description: Every market serving the pair that is open to new positions, one entry per market, each under its own `marketId`: a venue with several markets on the pair appears once for each.

MarginVenueMarket.description: One market serving the pair, for the advanced breakdown. A venue can list several, each its own entry under its own `marketId`. The row's `maxLeverage` is the HEADLINE market's: the `venueMarkets` entry with the greatest `maxLeverage`, the first listed on a tie. `headlineMarketId` names it, and `headlineVenue` names only its venue, which several entries can share.

venueMarketId.description: Morpho's own market id, for display and links. Absent where the (adapter, pair) IS the market. Never an input: an `open` names its market by `marketId`.

maxLeverage.description: Decimal string: the leverage of the lower of two ceilings, the venue's liquidation LTV (`lltv`) held back by the LTV cliff buffer, and the LTV the venue lends at held back by 1 bps. On Aave v3 the lending LTV is the reserve's own, which can sit well under `lltv`; on Morpho and Aave v4 it is the liquidation LTV itself, so the cliff-buffered side binds. A venue that lends nothing against the collateral is left off the row. Server-authored: a client must not compute this from `lltv`, or its ceiling and the quote's refusal disagree. The policy ceiling, not a guarantee: once its swap is priced, an `open` or `increaseLeverage` near it is served at the leverage its worst-case fill can reach, below this. Note the buffer SCALES the ceiling rather than subtracting from it, so 86% at 400bps is 82.56% and not 82%.

lltv.description: The liquidation boundary itself, 18-decimal fixed point. One side of the ceiling `maxLeverage` comes from, never the borrow limit by itself.

borrowRate.description: Annual borrow rate, 18-decimal fixed point. Read from chain through the same function `POST /margin/quote` reads it through. Absent when the venue's rate read failed, which is not a rate of zero.

availableBorrowLiquidity.description: What the venue can actually lend, in raw debt-token units. On Aave this is `min(virtual balance, borrow cap - debt - the interest that debt can accrue in 912 s)`: the cap usually binds first, so the balance alone overstates it. On `AAVE_V4` it is the hub's `getAssetLiquidity` for the debt asset, held under what the spoke's draw cap still lets it draw once the interest its owed debt, premium included, can accrue in 912 s is set aside. Absent when the read failed.

marketId.description: The market's id: what `open.marketId` names on `POST /margin/quote` to open on exactly this market.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page, which is how a client knows to stop. Present means more rows exist, never that the next page is non-empty.

MarginMarketsResponse.description: A page of markets. Rows are in a total order over (exposureToken, counterToken, direction), so a token's rows are contiguous and a cursor resolves to the same row across a catalogue rebuild.

MarginAssetPair.description: One (exposureToken, counterToken) pair within a direction.

venues.description: The venues the catalogue opens the pair on, never empty. A venue whose market is close-only, hard-triggered or stale is left off, and a pair no venue opens is not listed. A listed venue can still be refused on live reserve or router state, so `GET /margin/markets` and `POST /margin/quote` are authoritative for what opens.

longs.description: Exposure is the collateral, counter the debt.

shorts.description: Exposure is the debt, counter the collateral.

MarginAssetsResponse.description: Every pair the catalogue serves on the chain, in the readings `GET /margin/markets` serves: a USD stablecoin is never the exposure unless both legs are one (served as the LONG of its collateral), so a market with one or two stablecoin legs is listed once, a market with none in both lists. Each list is ordered by exposureToken address, then counterToken address.

MarginPositionStatus.description: `ACTIVE`: still open on chain, including a position that survived a partial liquidation. `COMPLETED`: the owner closed it, and it was never liquidated in that epoch. `PARTIALLY_LIQUIDATED`: the owner closed it after a partial liquidation earlier in the same epoch. `LIQUIDATED`: a liquidation cleared its debt; any collateral it left on the account is counted as returned, in `size` and `realizedPnl`.

MarginPositionRow.description: One position: a margin account (`swapper`, `subId`) on one venue and market.

size.description: Exposure in exposure-token base units: held now on an ACTIVE row, held when it closed on a terminal one.

subId.description: The account index every quote action key addresses.

account.description: The MarginAccount, derived offchain from (swapper, subId).

debtAmount.description: ACTIVE only. Raw debt-token units owed now.

depositedEquity.description: Raw collateral-token units deposited over the position's life. Absent when the store has not indexed the position or its flows went untracked.

entryPrice.description: Cost basis, from the position store: the average fill of the exposure bought and still held. A sale or partial liquidation takes what it sold at that average and a withdrawal of the owner's own equity takes nothing, so none of them moves it; a later buy averages in with what is still held. In the same terms as `oraclePrice`: counter per exposure, 1e18-scaled, reciprocated on a SHORT. Absent when the store has not indexed the position or it recorded no buy.

openedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds of the open, from the position store. Absent when the store has not indexed the position.

accruedInterest.description: Interest accrued on the debt, in raw debt-token units. ACTIVE rows: interest up to the last position event plus live growth since. Terminal rows: lifetime interest. Absent when any leg predates interest tracking.

unrealizedPnl.description: ACTIVE only. Raw collateral-token units: current equity plus collateral already returned, minus collateral deposited. Absent when the store has not indexed the position or it has no recorded deposit.

roe.description: ACTIVE only. `unrealizedPnl` / `depositedEquity`, 1e18-scaled, signed. Absent when either is.

equity.description: Collateral net of debt, the debt valued at `currentPrice`, or at the venue mark when `currentPrice` is absent, in COLLATERAL-token base units: the exposure token on a LONG, the counter token on a SHORT, so scale it by that token's decimals. `leverage`, `unrealizedPnl`, `roe` and `unrealizedPnlInDebt` are valued at the same price. Absent when no price could be read.

leverage.description: Collateral over equity, as a decimal string (`"1.83"`): the encoding `POST /margin/quote` serves as `display.leverage` and reads back as a leverage target, never a raw WAD integer. Valued at the same price as `equity`. Absent when `equity` is zero at that price, as there is no finite leverage, or when `equity` is absent and the LTV is at or above 1. Absent leverage does not mean liquidatable: `healthFactor` is measured at `oraclePrice` and can still be above 1e18 when `currentPrice` alone leaves no equity.

oraclePrice.description: The position's VENUE mark, in trader terms. This is the price risk is measured against, and it is not the price a swap would fill at.

currentPrice.description: ACTIVE only. The market price the position is marked at: `equity`, `leverage`, `unrealizedPnl`, `roe` and `unrealizedPnlInDebt` are valued at it. It can differ from `oraclePrice`, which risk is measured against. Counter per exposure, 1e18-scaled, in the same trader terms as `oraclePrice`. Unlike `oraclePrice` and the risk fields, it can be served from a short-lived cache. Absent when none was read; those fields are then valued at `oraclePrice`.

liquidationPrice.description: In trader terms. `oraclePrice / liquidationPrice` equals `healthFactor` on a LONG; on a SHORT, where both prices are reciprocated, `liquidationPrice / oraclePrice` does.

buffer.description: How far the mark can move before the position liquidates, as a WAD fraction of the mark. Zero at or past liquidation, never negative: `healthFactor` says how far past.

borrowRate.description: The venue's annual borrow rate, 1e18-scaled. Absent when the rate read failed, never zero.

maxWithdrawable.description: Collateral that can be withdrawn while staying under the BUFFERED ceiling, the lower of the liquidation LTV less the LTV cliff buffer and the LTV the venue lends at, with headroom for the interest and price drift before the withdraw lands, so withdrawing all of it does not revert. A `withdrawEquity` quote still takes this amount after interest has accrued since it was read; a price move against the position since the read can refuse it with a 422 `MARGIN_LEVERAGE_EXCEEDS_MAX`, so read it again then. A position with no debt can withdraw all of it. It is also held to what the venue pays out at the block read: `0` while the collateral reserve is paused or no longer active (or, on Aave v4, while the hub halts the spoke), and never more than the collateral the venue holds unlent. Absent when an Aave v3 venue's reserve LTV did not read. Do not recompute it from `lltv`.

exitPrice.description: Terminal only. The close's swap price, or the liquidation's, in the same terms as `entryPrice`. Absent when nothing was sold.

realizedPnl.description: Terminal only. Raw collateral-token units: collateral returned over the position's life minus collateral deposited. On a liquidation, collateral left on the account after the seizure counts as returned. Absent for positions closed outside the router, and for liquidations whose collateral was not tracked.

unrealizedPnlInDebt.description: ACTIVE only. `unrealizedPnl` in raw debt-token units, with each deposit and return valued at the venue's oracle mark at its event; `entryPrice` and `exitPrice` are the swap fills. The dollar PnL on a LONG against a stablecoin. Absent when any deposit or return could not be priced.

realizedPnlInDebt.description: Terminal only. `realizedPnl` in raw debt-token units, valued the same way, with a liquidation's leftover at the liquidation's price. Absent when any deposit or return could not be priced.

openTxHash.description: The tx that opened the position.

closeTxHash.description: Terminal only. The tx that closed the position; a full liquidation is its own close.

lastLiquidationTxHash.description: The latest liquidation, partial or full. On an ACTIVE row it means the position survived a partial liquidation.

collateralAtOpen.description: Raw collateral-token units held right after the open. Absent when the store did not record it.

activityId.description: The lifecycle `GET /margin/positions/activity` serves every event of. Absent for a position the store has not indexed, or indexed before it kept lifecycles.

costBasisInDebt.description: ACTIVE only. Raw debt-token units: the basis of the equity still in the position, each deposit valued at the venue's oracle mark at its event. Each withdrawal removes the share of the basis it takes of the equity, both at the withdrawal's price. Absent like `unrealizedPnlInDebt`.

realizedPnlToDateInDebt.description: ACTIVE only. Raw debt-token units, signed: what withdrawals so far fetched above the basis they removed.

MarginActivityKind.description: `MARGIN_ACTIVITY_KIND_LIQUIDATION` is a liquidation, partial or full; a full one also ends the lifecycle. `MARGIN_ACTIVITY_KIND_CLOSE` is the end of the lifecycle by any other means, or, after a liquidation that left nothing, the end that liquidation caused, found at the reopen. `MARGIN_ACTIVITY_KIND_ADJUSTMENT` is a move the store could not attribute, such as an owner action outside the router or a re-anchor to the chain: it carries no amounts, only the position it left.

at.description: Epoch milliseconds, as a decimal string: proto3 JSON writes int64 as a string.

collateralSold.description: A partial decrease: raw collateral-token units sold.

debtRepaid.description: A partial decrease: raw debt-token units repaid.

equityDeposited.description: Raw collateral-token units the owner put in, as the row's `depositedEquity` counts them: a deposit of the debt token at the venue's mark.

equityWithdrawn.description: Raw collateral-token units returned to the owner, counted the same way.

price.description: The fill of the event's buy, sale, close or full liquidation, in the same terms as the row's `entryPrice`. Absent when the event has none.

collateralAfter.description: Raw collateral-token units the event left on the position.

debtAfter.description: Raw debt-token units the event left owed.

entryPrice.description: The position's entry price as the event left it, in the same terms as the row's `entryPrice`. Absent until the lifecycle has bought.

activity.description: Oldest first. Empty for an `activityId` the store holds nothing for.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page, which is how a client knows to stop. Present means more entries may exist, never that the next page is non-empty.

MarginPendingPlan.description: The one plan-store read, and a deliberately weaker guarantee than the rest of this response: session-scoped and TTL-bound, so absent rather than wrong once a row ages out. Acceptable only because no funds are at risk in that state.

createdAt.description: Epoch milliseconds. Rendered as a string by proto3 JSON; the client does not sort on it.

currentStep.description: 0-based index of the first step that is not COMPLETE.

cancellable.description: False once an in-progress step carries a proof: that transaction may have landed, so cancelling could strand what it moved.

MarginPositionsResponse.description: A page of positions. Rows are in a total order over (exposureToken, counterToken, direction), the same order the markets feed uses.

nextCursor.description: Absent on the last page, which is how a client knows to stop. Present means more rows exist, never that the next page is non-empty.

pendingPlans.description: The margin plans this swapper started and has not finished, newest first, so a client can offer to resume or cancel one. Terminal plans are excluded server-side, and so is a plan whose execute deadline has passed, since its MARGIN_EXECUTE can only revert; one with an in-progress step carrying a proof stays, uncancellable, because that transaction may have landed. Served on the first page only: a request carrying `cursor` gets [] here, so concatenating pages never repeats a plan. Serializes as [] when the read ran and found nothing; it cannot express "not read", so a degraded plan-store read logs a warning and reports empty rather than failing the page.

MarginTokenMetadata.description: A token as a response carries it. No symbol or name: this endpoint resolves markets, not token metadata, and a client merges display fields from its own token lists by address.

MarginVenue.description: A lending venue the position can be held at.

MarginEquityAction.description:
`addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`. Size is held and leverage follows, so no leverage target.

`amount` is denominated in `walletToken` on `addEquity` and in the COLLATERAL token on `withdrawEquity`. That asymmetry is deliberate: how much collateral can leave before health hits the floor is answerable from the position alone, so denominating a withdrawal in `walletToken` would make whether it is allowed move with the funding route. It also matches the on-chain primitive, which takes a collateral amount.

MarginEquityLeverageAction.description: The four composites. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried.

amount.description: The equity magnitude, in `walletToken`'s native decimals.

MarginLeverageAction.description: `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`. Equity is held, so no amount.

MarginLeverageLeg.description: The LEVERAGE leg's controls: the flash-accounted, debt-funded swap inside the router. Required on every action that moves leverage, and forbidden on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which hold size and let leverage follow.

slippageTolerance.description: The leverage leg's tolerance, always an explicit percentage from 0 to 5, the widest tolerance `POST /plan` derives the bounds at, so a quote never sizes the leverage bought at a tolerance the plan does not apply. Independent of `swapConfig.slippageTolerance`; neither defaults from the other. There is deliberately no `autoSlippage` counterpart here, because this tolerance derives `maxDebtIn`/`maxCollateralIn`, which stamp into calldata as the MEV backstop, and a routing heuristic must not size a binding fund-safety bound.

MarginOpenAction.description: `open`. No `positionId`: the server allocates one when the plan's margin step is served.

amount.description: The equity magnitude, in `walletToken`'s native decimals.

marketId.description: The market to open on, as `GET /margin/markets` lists it in `venueMarkets[].marketId`. The quote prices this market alone and never moves the open to another market or venue. A missing or malformed id is a 400 `RequestValidationError`; one that names no market `GET /margin/markets` lists on `positionChainId` is a 422 `MARGIN_MARKET_NOT_FOUND`; one whose market is not the request's pair on the side `direction` puts it is a 400 `MARGIN_MARKET_MISMATCH`; one whose market `direction` reads in a way `GET /margin/markets` does not list it, a USD stablecoin as the exposure against a volatile token or the `SHORT` of a stablecoin against a stablecoin, is a 400 `MARGIN_MIRRORED_READING`; and one on a market closed to new positions is a 422 `MARGIN_NO_ELIGIBLE_VENUE`.

MarginPositionAction.description: `close`. The whole position, so structurally neither a leverage target nor an amount.

MarginProtocols.description: The AMM allowlist for the swap legs. Only Uniswap AMM protocols are eligible: a margin leg is flash-accounted inside the router, so UniswapX order types cannot serve it. Applies when the quote is priced: the funding swap `POST /plan` builds routes over V2, V3 and V4 pools without hooks whatever this list named.

MarginQuoteAddEquityAndDecreaseLeverageR.description: Add equity and lower leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteAddEquityAndIncreaseLeverageR.description: Add equity and raise leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteAddEquityRequest.description: Add equity and let leverage fall. Size is held, so there is no leverage swap to bound. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage is not targeted, so the top-level `slippageTolerance` is forbidden. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

Equity is held, so nothing crosses the wallet boundary. `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are forbidden. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteOpenRequest.description: Open a new position. The server allocates the position id when the plan's margin step is served, so no `positionId` is sent. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteRequest.description:
Prices one margin action. The request is the shared block plus EXACTLY ONE of the ten action keys: `open`, `close`, `increaseLeverage`, `decreaseLeverage`, `addEquity`, `withdrawEquity`, `addEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `addEquityAndDecreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquityAndIncreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquityAndDecreaseLeverage`. Sending none of them, or more than one, is rejected: both are structural, not field-presence rules applied after the fact.

Every field inside an action key is required, so what a caller must send follows entirely from which action it is doing. There are no optional fields inside a key and no field whose absence carries meaning.

Two shared blocks are required-or-forbidden per key, never optional. The wallet block (`walletToken`, `walletChainId`, `swapConfig`) is forbidden on `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`, which hold equity, and required on the other eight. The top-level `slippageTolerance`, the leverage leg's, is forbidden on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which hold size, and required on the other eight. Each variant below states its own rule.

Amounts are decimal strings in the token's native decimals. Leverage is a decimal string. Prices, the liquidation health factors and borrow rates are unsuffixed 18-decimal fixed point.

Unknown fields are rejected with a 400 rather than ignored, so a retired or misspelled field fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing. This cannot be stated in the schema itself: the variants compose their shared blocks with `allOf`, and `additionalProperties: false` under `allOf` would reject the very fields the sibling blocks contribute.

MarginQuoteRequestBase.description: The fields every margin action sends, whichever action key it uses. Never sent on its own: a request is one of the ten `MarginQuote*Request` variants, each of which is this block plus its action key and that key's required peers.

positionChainId.description: The chain the POSITION lives on. Named rather than left as a bare `chainId` because two chains are in play: with one of them unqualified a client reasonably reads it as "the" chain, sets it to the chain it is paying from, and silently gets a cross-chain funding flow it never asked for.

exposureToken.description: The token the position is exposed to. Which side of the market this is depends on `direction`, never on the order of the pair.

counterToken.description: The other side of the market. Which side of the market this is depends on `direction`, never on the order of the pair.

MarginQuoteWithdrawEquityAndDecreaseLeve.description: Withdraw equity and lower leverage in one action. Both axes move, so both magnitudes are carried. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage moves, so the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance` is required. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginQuoteWithdrawEquityRequest.description: Withdraw equity and let leverage rise. Size is held, so there is no leverage swap to bound. `amount` here is denominated in the COLLATERAL token, not `walletToken`; the one place the "amount is always walletToken" rule breaks. Equity crosses the wallet boundary, so `walletToken`, `walletChainId` and `swapConfig` are required. Leverage is not targeted, so the top-level `slippageTolerance` is forbidden. The nine other action keys are forbidden, which is what makes EXACTLY ONE enforceable: the ten `oneOf` branches alone do not say it, because a pair drawn from two different peer-rule groups (say `open` with `increaseLeverage`) matches exactly one branch.

MarginSwapConfig.description:
Execution policy for the WALLET-side swap, and nothing else. It names no token, no chain, no amount and no trade type: identity lives at the top level in `walletToken`/`walletChainId`, the magnitude lives in the action key, and exact-in versus exact-out follows from whether the action pays in or pays out.

`slippageTolerance` is required and at most 5, the widest tolerance `POST /plan` builds the swap at. `autoSlippage` is refused by name with a `RequestValidationError`, as on the leverage leg: this tolerance derives that floor, and a resolved auto-slippage value is not visible to the sizing path.

Kept separate from `walletToken` because the two have different lifetimes: `walletToken` is always meaningful, while this block can be moot, since paying in the collateral token needs no funding swap at all and whether one is needed is a routing outcome not knowable at request time.

Funding from another chain applies only `slippageTolerance`: its route is priced at `BEST_PRICE` over v2, v3 and v4 pools whatever `routingPreference` and `protocols` say.

slippageTolerance.description: The WALLET-side swap’s tolerance, from 0 to 5. Derives `funding.output.minimumAmount`, which is the equity the position is sized on — not `funding.output.amount`.

routingPreference.description: Defaults to `BEST_PRICE`, matching every other quote in this API. This leg is the slowest call in a margin quote, and `FASTEST` takes roughly a second off it for a handful of basis points -- which `slippageTolerance` already floors before the position is sized. Send `FASTEST` when the quote is indicative and the latency matters more than the last few bps.

MarginWalletBlock.description: The wallet-side block: the token crossing the wallet boundary, where it sits, and how its swap should execute. Required in full on every action that moves equity, and forbidden in full on `increaseLeverage` and `decreaseLeverage`, which hold equity. It is never genuinely optional: whether it applies follows from the action key alone.

walletToken.description: The token crossing the wallet boundary. Deliberately not named `tokenIn`: `close` and the `withdrawEquity*` keys pay OUT, so an "in" name would be wrong on four of the ten keys. Flow direction is read off the action key and never restated here. The action key's `amount` is denominated in this token, except on `withdrawEquity`.

walletChainId.description: Where `walletToken` sits. Differing from `positionChainId` means cross-chain funding, which is pay-in only (`open`, `addEquity` and the two add-equity composites) and served from a chain Across bridges from.

marginLeverage.description: Leverage as a decimal string (`"3"`, `"2.55"`), never a number. Leverage is money-adjacent, so it is carried as a string to keep it out of float rounding. Must be greater than 1: leverage buys collateral with borrowed funds, so 1x buys nothing and opens no position. Rejected at the boundary rather than deep in sizing.

marginMarketId.description: A margin market's id, 0x-prefixed 32-byte hex, as `GET /margin/markets` lists it in lowercase: `0x` followed by the sha256 of the UTF-8 string `<chainId>:<venue>:<venueMarketId>`, where `venue` is `morpho_blue`, `aave_v3` or `aave_v4` and `venueMarketId` is the venue's own id for the market in lowercase: Morpho's market id on Morpho, the one the listing serves as `venueMarkets[].venueMarketId`, `<collateral>:<debt>` on Aave v3, and `<spoke>:<collateralReserveId>:<debtReserveId>` on Aave v4. It names one market exactly. Take it from the listing rather than building it.

marginPositionId.description: The id of an existing margin position, as a decimal integer string with no leading zeros, at most 2^256 - 1 (the router's uint256 subId). Absent on `open`, where the server allocates it when the plan's margin step is served.

marginFixedPoint18.description: An unsuffixed 18-decimal fixed-point value as an integer string: divide by 10^18 to read it. Prices, the liquidation buffer, health factors, borrow rates, LTVs and equity shares all use this scale regardless of the tokens' own decimals. Every field on this scale is non-negative, `buffer` included: it is a distance to liquidation, not a signed move.

MarginIntent.description: The action that was priced, carried as the proto enum's full member name (`MARGIN_INTENT_OPEN`, not `OPEN`). Mirrors the request's action key one to one, so a client can tell what it got without re-deriving it from its own request, and matches the vocabulary of the `MARGIN_INTENT_MISMATCH` error and the plan steps. Always present, including at its default `MARGIN_INTENT_OPEN`.

MarginOperationType.description: One on-chain call inside the router's `execute([...actions])` stream. Which fields of the operation are set follows from this type. `INCREASE_POSITION` buys collateral with borrowed debt; `DECREASE_POSITION` sells collateral to repay debt; `ADD_COLLATERAL` and `WITHDRAW` move collateral across the wallet boundary without swapping; `SWEEP` carries no fields and returns whatever a `close`'s deliberate debt over-buy did not need, so the dust is not stranded in a position the caller believes is gone.

MarginOperation.description: The confirmed bounds for one operation. Which fields are set follows from `type`; they are the numbers that stamp into router calldata, so token amounts are in the token's native decimals while LTV and prices are 18-decimal fixed point.

type.description: Which on-chain router call this operation compiles to. Always present.

collateralToBuy.description: `INCREASE_POSITION` only: the exact-out buy of the collateral asset.

maxDebtIn.description: `INCREASE_POSITION` only: the binding cap on debt spent, the expected debt padded UP by the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance`, and the most `POST /plan` will stamp: a re-priced fill above it is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_PRICE_DRIFT`. Mandatory and non-zero on-chain, since the router refuses a zero bound outright; a fill too small to bound is refused as a 422 `MARGIN_SWAP_INSUFFICIENT_LIQUIDITY`. Derived from the top-level tolerance and never from `swapConfig`'s, so widening the wallet-side swap cannot loosen the MEV backstop.

debtToRepay.description: `DECREASE_POSITION` only: the debt cleared at the venue. On `close` this deliberately EXCEEDS the debt read at quote time by the projected accrual over the inclusion window, so the repay does not come up short and revert; the trailing `SWEEP` returns the excess. On a `close` of a position that owes nothing it is `"0"`, as is `maxCollateralIn`, and no `SWEEP` follows: nothing is sold, and the router withdraws the whole balance as it stands when the transaction lands. On any other key it never exceeds what the position owes, and `POST /plan` refuses an echo the position no longer owes in full with a 422 `MARGIN_POSITION_CHANGED`, since a partial decrease returns none of the debt token it bought beyond the debt.

maxCollateralIn.description: `DECREASE_POSITION` only: the cap on collateral sold to raise `debtToRepay`, padded UP by the leverage leg's `slippageTolerance`, and the most `POST /plan` will stamp. A re-priced fill above it is refused with a 422 `MARGIN_PRICE_DRIFT`, on `close` as on a partial decrease, since the router reverts a sale that needs more than this cap.

maxLtvAfter.description: The health assertion the router checks AFTER executing, so the calldata enforces the ceiling the quote refused to cross rather than trusting the fill to respect it. A leg that sells to repay carries the liquidation LTV less the cliff buffer, unless the same action withdraws; any other carries the borrow-side ceiling, or that same liquidation side where the venue lends nothing, because a zero bound makes the router skip its check. Set on every operation of the equity keys and the six leverage-target keys; absent on `open`, on `close` and on `SWEEP`.

amount.description: `ADD_COLLATERAL` and `WITHDRAW` only: the magnitude in the collateral token, always positive, since the direction is the operation's own. On an add that was funded by a wallet-side swap or a route from another chain this is the funding's FLOOR (`funding.output.minimumAmount`, which a route from another chain also reports as `funding.minBridgeOut`) rather than its expected output, because collateral the funding does not deliver is collateral the venue never receives.

minHopPrice.description: Optional per-hop bound; `"0"` disables it. 18-decimal on the wire, X36 at encode. Not populated today.

effectivePrice.description: This operation's quoted fill. Reported only: `POST /plan` measures drift against `maxDebtIn` and `maxCollateralIn`, not against this. On the venue's own (collateral, debt) orientation, debt per collateral, so a short's reads inverted relative to `display.effectivePrice`. Present on `INCREASE_POSITION` and `DECREASE_POSITION`, the two operations that swap; absent on the rest, and on the `DECREASE_POSITION` of a `close` that owes nothing, which swaps nothing.

MarginExecutionLeg.description: One venue's share of the action, as an ordered list of on-chain operations. One venue carries the whole position today, so `legs` has exactly one entry.

venue.description: The lending venue this leg routes to. Always present, including at its default `MORPHO`.

subId.description: Server-resolved on the manage keys, where it is the `positionId` the request addressed. Absent on `open`, whose sub-account is allocated when the plan's margin step is served, and `POST /plan` refuses an `open` echo that carries one.

operations.description: Ordered, in the sequence they execute. One on the simple keys. A composite populates more than one, with the equity side on opposite ends depending on which way it moves: a supply (`ADD_COLLATERAL`) goes FIRST, because it strictly lowers LTV, and a withdrawal (`WITHDRAW`) goes LAST, matching what the router does. `close` is a `DECREASE_POSITION` followed by a `SWEEP`.

marketId.description: On `open` only: the market the quote priced, `open.marketId` in lowercase, which `POST /plan` opens on. Absent on the manage keys, whose market is the position's.

MarginFunding.description: The wallet-side funding as priced, in the same shape `/quote` uses for an ordinary swap, so the funding leg reads natively rather than inventing a fourth swap-quote vocabulary. Present IFF funding was actually priced: a swap on the position's chain, or a route from `walletChainId` when it differs from `positionChainId`. A route from another chain is one chained route: an optional swap on the source chain, an Across bridge, and, when the collateral is the wrapped native token and Across pays the swapper in native currency (a wallet with no code or an EIP-7702 delegation), a WRAP on the position's chain; its equity is fixed at `minBridgeOut`, the guaranteed floor, and is not resized when the funds land. `output.minimumAmount` is the equity the position was SIZED on, not `output.amount`: collateral the swap does not deliver is collateral the venue never receives. Carries no `protocols` and no `autoSlippage`: the first was a request echo that no consumer read and that could not express absence, and the second is a request-side mode whose only useful answer is the percent it resolved to, which `slippageTolerance` already carries.

tokenInChainId.description: Where `walletToken` sits. Differs from `positionChainId` when the funding comes from another chain.

input.description: The caller's spend in `walletToken`. Exact-in, so `maximumAmount` equals `amount`.

output.description: The collateral bought. `minimumAmount` is the floor the position is sized against; `recipient` is the `swapper`.

slippageTolerance.description: The wallet-side tolerance the floor was derived at, which `POST /plan` re-derives against. Echoed from `swapConfig.slippageTolerance`, which is required in practice today since `autoSlippage` is not resolved yet.

minBridgeOut.description: Cross-chain pay-in only: the guaranteed bridge floor, Across's output for the source swap's minimum output, or for `input.amount` when the route starts with the bridge, less 10 bps held back against a relay fee that rises before the deposit fills. `output.amount` holds back the same 10 bps from Across's output for the source swap's expected output. Equal to `output.minimumAmount`, which the position is sized on.

priceImpact.description: How far this swap lands from the pool's price, as a percent, exactly as `/quote` reports it. Reported, never refused: this leg spends the caller's own funds at the tolerance they chose, unlike the leverage leg, whose impact is multiplied by leverage and is refused past a ceiling with a 422 `MARGIN_SWAP_PRICE_IMPACT`. Absent when the quote carried no measurement, which is not the same as zero.

steps.description: The funding's steps in order, as `/quote` reports a chained route's: the approvals the swapper still needs, then the route. Present whenever this block is. The approvals (`RESET_APPROVAL_TXN`, `APPROVAL_TXN`, `APPROVAL_PERMIT`) are decided from the swapper's allowances when the quote is priced, by the rule `POST /plan` applies, so a wallet already approved shows none. On the position's chain the route is a `CLASSIC` swap, or a `WRAP` of native currency into a wrapped-native collateral; from another chain it is an optional swap on the source chain, the `BRIDGE`, and a `WRAP` on the position's chain when Across pays the collateral as native currency. Steps carry no amounts: `output`, and `minBridgeOut` from another chain, are what the funding delivers.

timeEstimateMs.description: Cross-chain pay-in only: estimated milliseconds to complete the funding steps.

gasFeeUsd.description: Cross-chain pay-in only: the estimated gas of every funding step, on both chains, in USD.

MarginExecution.description: Everything `POST /plan` needs, and nothing it does not. This subtree is what a client echoes back to create a plan; `display` never is.

direction.description: Echoed from the request. Always present, including at its default `LONG`.

intent.description: Which action was priced, derived from the request's action key. Always present.

leverageTarget.description: Echoed from the request. Present iff the action key names a leverage target: `open` and the six leverage-target keys. Absent on `close`, `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`.

slippageTolerance.description: The leverage leg's confirmed tolerance, echoed from the top-level `slippageTolerance`. Absent on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which forbid it because they price no leverage leg. There is no AMM allowlist beside it: the leverage leg is v4 by construction, so it could not honour one; the wallet-side swap carries its own in the request's `swapConfig.protocols`.

funding.description: The wallet-side funding as priced. Present IFF funding was priced, so its presence is the signal that funding happened: a swap on the position's chain, or a route from `walletChainId` when it differs from `positionChainId`. Absent when the action moves no equity in (`close`, `increaseLeverage`, `decreaseLeverage`, `withdrawEquity` and the two withdraw composites), and absent when `walletToken` already IS the position's collateral on the position's chain, since paying in the collateral itself needs no funding and a block whose input and output name the same token and amount describes no trade.

legs.description: Always present. One entry today: a single venue carries the whole position.

MarginDisplay.description:
What the confirmation modal renders: projections of the position IF this action executes. Present state lives on the positions read, not here. Ignored by `POST /plan`: projections are not execution inputs.

Two prices, never mixed: `oraclePrice` is the venue's own mark and drives every risk output, while `effectivePrice` is what the leverage swap realizes and drives sizing. They differ by the spread, and substituting one for the other sizes a position against a figure the swap will not achieve.

On every action that prices a leverage leg, `leverage`, `liquidationPrice` and `healthFactor` describe the position the WORST fill the leg's bound allows leaves: the debt `maxDebtIn` lets the swap spend, or the collateral `maxCollateralIn` lets it sell, valued at `oraclePrice` and rounded against the caller, and never past the operation's `maxLtvAfter`, above which the router reverts. At that mark, and before the debt accrues further, any fill inside the tolerance lands at that risk or less; the positions read reports where it landed.

A `close` describes a position that will not exist, so it reports `size` `"0"`, `effectivePrice` (absent when the position owes nothing, since nothing is sold), `oraclePrice`, `collateralReturned` and `debtRepaid` only: no leverage, liquidation price, buffer, health factor or borrow rate, because zeroes there would read as real, and `legs` is `[]`.

size.description: Exposure asset, native decimals, summed across legs. `"0"` on `close`.

leverage.description: Position over equity as a decimal string. On `open` and the six leverage-target keys it is the leverage at the worst fill the leverage leg's bound allows, so it differs from the request's target, which `execution.leverageTarget` echoes, by what the fill can cost against the mark, and sits below it where `open` or `increaseLeverage` was served below a target whose worst-case fill would land past the health ceiling the router asserts. It is DERIVED from the position on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, where leverage follows from the collateral moving. Absent on `close`.

effectivePrice.description: The quoted fill including fees, impact and slippage, size-weighted across legs. A property of a swap, so it is absent on `addEquity` and `withdrawEquity`, which perform none: reporting the mark there would be the exact substitution this field exists to prevent. In TRADER terms (counter per exposure): on a short, the reciprocal of the operation's `effectivePrice`.

liquidationPrice.description: The oracle price at which LTV reaches LLTV, from the same worst fill as `leverage`. Multi-leg: the nearest leg's, because legs liquidate independently. Absent on `close`. In TRADER terms (counter per exposure), the same frame as `oraclePrice` and `effectivePrice`.

healthFactor.description: collateral x LLTV / debt, at the same worst fill as `leverage`; liquidatable below 1, that is below `"1000000000000000000"`. Nearest leg. The one risk number that normalizes across venues, so it is what a client bands into Healthy / Caution / Risky; the band thresholds are a product call and stay client-side. Absent on `close`.

borrowRate.description: Annualized borrow rate on the debt, size-weighted across legs. Absent when the selected venue's rate read supplied none, and on `close`.

oraclePrice.description: The venue's liquidation-reference price, in TRADER terms (counter per exposure): reciprocated on a short, the same frame as `effectivePrice` and `liquidationPrice`.

collateralReturned.description: `close` only: the collateral handed back after the router has sold what `maxCollateralIn` allows to buy the debt back. The floor of the payout, since the cap is padded against the caller.

debtRepaid.description: `close` only: the debt the position owed as read, which is what the close clears. Smaller than the operation's `debtToRepay`, whose excess the `SWEEP` returns.

MarginQuoteResponse.description:
A priced margin action. `execution` is what `POST /plan` consumes; `display` is what the confirmation modal renders and is ignored by `/plan`.

Every enum field is serialized, including at its protobuf default value, so an absent enum never has to be read as a default, and every `repeated` field is serialized, as `[]` when empty. `optional` fields are absent when unset.

gasEstimate.description: Indicative gas estimate for the resulting plan, and INDICATIVE is the operative word: the transaction does not exist at quote time, so there is no calldata to estimate against. Exactly one of `eip1559` and `legacy` is set. `gasLimit` is sized, not estimated against calldata, and sums the margin step's limit and the funding transaction's. The margin step's is per intent, venue and the shape of the leverage leg's route (its protocol and hop count), raised when the route's quoter measured more swap gas at this size than the shape's floor, with 30% headroom and never under 1,100,000 on a `close`, or per intent alone on an action with no leverage leg. When `funding` is present the funding transaction's is added: the wallet-side swap's routed gas with 30% headroom and never under 300,000, or 250,000 for a wrap. On funding from another chain only the position chain's part is added, which is 250,000 for the WRAP when Across pays native currency and nothing otherwise; the source chain's steps are priced in `funding.gasFeeUsd` instead. Approvals the plan may add are not counted; `maxFeePerGas` and `maxPriorityFeePerGas` are live network readings. No `strategy` is served: the fee comes from an urgency path that returns none, so any strategy shown would describe an algorithm that did not run. Absent entirely when the gas oracle is unavailable, which does not fail the quote.

SwapSource.description: Where the input tokens come from. Leave unset (or send "WALLET") to pull them from the swapper's wallet as usual. Send "UNIVERSAL_ROUTER" to get calldata that swaps whatever balance of the input token the Universal Router holds when it runs, for bridge-and-swap flows where a bridge deposits into the router and executes the swap in the same transaction. In this mode, quote on the destination chain, use `amount` as your estimate of what will arrive, and put the end user in `swapper`. Exact-input, single-chain, AMM-only swaps: `protocols` defaults to V2/V3/V4 and a UniswapX protocol is rejected with a 400. With a native input, V4 is left out of the route whenever V2 or V3 is allowed: the router can only spend native ETH through a route that first wraps it to WETH, and a V4 pool that takes native ETH directly can't be encoded. A V4-only request is routed as asked. The returned transaction has no `from` (the executing filler is unknown) and a `value` of "0"; with a native input the filler must attach the delivered ETH as msg.value. The output floor is fixed at quote time from `amount` minus `slippageTolerance`: if less than `amount` arrives, the whole balance is still swapped and must clear that floor, so a delivery short by more than the tolerance reverts even without `enforceExactIn`. Use a conservative `amount` or widen `slippageTolerance`. `generatePermitAsTransaction` is rejected with a 400. Works on both /quote and /swap. A failed simulation only refuses the request when the verdict applies to a router-funded fill: a revert, or a simulation that could not run. A slippage flag, or a failure to pull from the quoted swapper, still returns calldata. Read the guide before using it: https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/trading/swapping-api/start-building/integration-guide#swapping-funds-already-in-the-universal-router

EnforceExactIn.description: Only with swapSource "UNIVERSAL_ROUTER". Set it to true when your bridge guarantees how much will arrive; the calldata then checks the router's balance and reverts if it holds less than `amount`. Leave it off if `amount` is just an estimate, or a good fill can revert over a small shortfall. Details: https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/trading/swapping-api/start-building/integration-guide#swapping-funds-already-in-the-universal-router

universalRouterVersionHeader.description: The version of the Universal Router the response was produced for. Always returned, whether the caller supplied `x-universal-router-version` on the request or the chain-specific default was applied.

agentInfoStatusHeader.description: Present, with the fixed value `malformed`, only when the request carried an `x-agent-info` header that failed to parse and was dropped; the value never echoes anything from the request. Absent when `x-agent-info` parsed, was not sent, or was sent with an empty value, which the gateway treats as not sent. Set by the API gateway once it has resolved the route and before it proxies the request, so it is returned on every response, including gateway-generated errors such as 400, 401, 403, and 429. It reports attribution only; the request itself succeeds or fails independently of it.

universalRouterVersionHeader.name: x-universal-router-version
universalRouterVersionHeader.description: The version of the Universal Router to use for the swap journey. *MUST* be consistent throughout the API calls.

erc20EthEnabledHeader.name: x-erc20eth-enabled
erc20EthEnabledHeader.description: Enable native ETH input support for UniswapX via ERC20-ETH (EIP-7914). When set to true and `tokenIn` is the native currency address (e.g. `0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`), the API may return UniswapX routes that spend native ETH for supported wallets.

permit2DisabledHeader.name: x-permit2-disabled
permit2DisabledHeader.description: Disables the Permit2 approval flow. When set to `true`, `permitData` is returned as `null` and the header is forwarded to the routing layer for correct gas simulation against the Proxy Universal Router contract. When `false` or omitted, the standard Permit2 approval flow is used. This header is intended for integrators whose infrastructure uses a direct approval-then-swap pattern without Permit2.

swapStepsEnabledHeader.name: x-universal-router-swapsteps
swapStepsEnabledHeader.description: Opts the request into Universal Router SwapSteps mode. Additive and opt-in: when set to `true`, the response's `ClassicQuote` may include a `swapSteps[]` array describing the Universal Router step sequence (the inputs to `SwapRouter.encodeSwaps`). The field is only populated when the GuideStar quoter wins the hybrid quote race (currently `EXACT_INPUT`; broader coverage will follow once UniRoute's transformer ships). Omitting or setting `false` preserves the existing response shape.

experimentalRoutingHeader.name: x-api-experimental
experimentalRoutingHeader.description: Opts the query into experimental behaviors. The behaviors this header enables are not part of the stable API contract and change over time without notice. Use it only in consultation with Uniswap: it may break existing customer integrations, and it may return invalid calldata or otherwise negatively impact the end-user swap experience. Omitting the header or setting it to `false` preserves standard behavior.

agentInfoHeader.name: x-agent-info
agentInfoHeader.description: Optional attribution hint for AI-agent traffic; send it if an AI agent built or operates your integration. The value is a JSON object with up to three fields: `decision_origin` (required, exactly `autonomous` or `human_mediated`, case-sensitive), `integration_name` (optional string naming your integration, e.g. `my-trading-bot`), and `version` (optional string identifying your integration's version). Any other key is dropped, never rejected. The raw value must be at most 1024 bytes of printable US-ASCII (`0x20`-`0x7E`), so send non-ASCII text as JSON `\u` escapes; `integration_name` and `version` are each limited to 256 UTF-16 code units and may not contain control characters, U+2028, U+2029, or U+FFFD. Send the header once: repeated header lines are joined with `, ` and the joined string is what gets parsed, so two complete objects fail as invalid JSON while a single object split across two lines still parses. The header is analytics-only and never affects the request: omitting it, sending it, or sending a value that fails these rules never changes the response status, body, or swap behavior. A value that fails to parse is dropped and reported by the `x-agent-info-status` response header. Never put a user ID, wallet address, email, session token, or API key in these fields.

orderTypeParam.name: orderType
orderTypeParam.description: The UniswapX order type to retrieve.

orderIdParam.name: orderId
orderIdParam.description: A transaction hash for an order. `orderId` or `orderIds` must be provided, but not both.

orderIdsParam.name: orderIds
orderIdsParam.description: A list of comma separated orderIds (transaction hashes). `orderId` or `orderIds` must be provided, but not both.

sortKeyParam.name: sortKey
sortKeyParam.description: Order the query results by the sort key.

transactionHashesParam.description: On-chain transaction hashes. At least one of `txHashes` or `userOpHashes` must be provided.
transactionHashesParam.name: txHashes

userOpHashesParam.description: ERC-4337 UserOperation hashes. At least one of `txHashes` or `userOpHashes` must be provided.
userOpHashesParam.name: userOpHashes

tokenListLimitParam.name: limit
tokenListLimitParam.description: Number of ranked tokens to return. Applies only when sort is `tvl` or `volume_24h`. Defaults to 100.
